stable.label: Defined in the released MCP specification

draft.label: Defined only in a draft revision of the MCP specification

proposed.label: Proposed, not yet in any published specification

deprecated.label: Defined in the released MCP specification but deprecated in this revision, and scheduled for removal in a later one

support_codes.y: present at the declared capture boundary
support_codes.a: changed at the boundary or retained elsewhere

defaults.inclusion_rule: A framework is listed if it ships a first-party or officially documented MCP adapter. Nothing is excluded on quality grounds.
defaults.order_rule: Alphabetical within language group. No ranking is implied or computed.
defaults.version_policy: Era 0 is the release actually measured. Surrounding releases come from the package registry (PyPI, npm) and are shown as not yet measured until a scan covers them.
defaults.green_rule: A cell is 'y' only if the value is present in the tool definition at that framework's declared capture boundary. Nothing else counts.
defaults.partial_rule: 'a' means the capability is not present unchanged: the note must say whether it was transformed at the boundary, only partly preserved, or retained elsewhere by the framework.
defaults.note_rule: Every 'a' and 'n' cell must carry a #n note reference naming the exact mechanism, so a status can be checked rather than trusted.
defaults.usage_rule: No adoption weighting is published. We have no defensible source yet, and an invented percentage would be the least trustworthy number on the page.

coverage.note: The feature surface of MCP 2025-11-25. Derived from the 2026-07-28 catalogue and that revision's official changelog, which enumerates every addition, removal and deprecation relative to this revision. This file is the denominator: what the protocol defines, independent of what we have measured.
omissions: Skills over MCP is not listed. The spec index advertises it, but /extensions/skills/overview 404s and the only published material is a working-group charter, so there is no wire contract to measure against.

Features removed in this revision (initialize, ping, logging/setLevel, resources/subscribe, notifications/roots/list_changed, Mcp-Session-Id, SSE resumability) are absent by design. They belong to the 2025-11-25 snapshot, not this one.

additional-properties.title: `additionalProperties`
additional-properties.description: Controls whether an object accepts keys that are not declared in its properties map.
additional-properties.question: Is each object's additional-properties policy preserved at the capture boundary?
additional-properties.notes: 26 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 5 changed or retained elsewhere, 0 dropped. A framework that regenerates the input schema from its own model class can change additionalProperties on the root and nested object schemas.
additional-properties.summary: A framework that regenerates the input schema from its own model class can change additionalProperties on the root and nested object schemas.

notes_by_num.1: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: the ChatModel default `use_strict_tool_schema=True` runs `to_strict_json_schema` on the rebuilt input model, which adds `additionalProperties: false` to every object, including `create_report`, its `config` and each `sections` item, where the server set nothing.
notes_by_num.2: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench.list_tools` rebuilds each schema as `ParametersSchema(properties, required, additionalProperties)` and defaults `additionalProperties` to `false` when the server omits it, so every tool gains a top-level `additionalProperties: false`.
notes_by_num.3: CrewAI: Pydantic model generation rewrites additionalProperties on several object boundaries, changing whether undeclared keys are accepted.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `convert_tools_to_openai_schema` emits the strict OpenAI function schema from the Pydantic `args_schema`, which sets `additionalProperties: false` on every object, including the ones the source left open.
notes_by_num.5: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): toolsFromDefinitions wraps each inputSchema as jsonSchema({...inputSchema, properties: inputSchema.properties ?? {}, additionalProperties: false}), so every tool's root object is closed to undeclared keys although the server set no policy there. Nested objects keep the server's policy.

default-value.title: `default`
default-value.description: Documents the value a server or client should assume when an optional parameter is omitted.
default-value.question: Is the declared default value preserved at each capture boundary?
default-value.notes: 28 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 0 changed or retained elsewhere, 3 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPTool._getDeclaration` passes `inputSchema` through `toGeminiSchema`, which keeps `type`, `description`, `enum`, `items`, `properties`, `required` and `anyOf` in the genai `Schema` dialect; `default` is not among them, so `search_records.limit`'s default never reaches the model.
notes_by_num.2: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpToolProvider` maps each `inputSchema` into LangChain4j's own `JsonSchemaElement` model (`JsonObjectSchema`, `JsonStringSchema`, `JsonIntegerSchema`, ...), and the `ToolSpecification` AiServices hands the `ChatModel` is built from that model. `JsonIntegerSchema` holds a description only, so `limit.default` is dropped.
notes_by_num.3: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `default` is dropped: `ToolParameterDescriptor` has no default slot, so `limit`'s default of 20 never reaches the model.

description-fidelity.title: `description`
description-fidelity.description: The natural-language description an MCP server publishes to explain what a tool does.
description-fidelity.question: Is the full tool description present at each capture boundary?
description-fidelity.notes: 28 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 3 changed or retained elsewhere, 0 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: the captured description is rebuilt as `Tool Name: ... Tool Arguments: {schema} Tool Description: ...`, duplicating the schema as prose and parameters.
notes_by_num.2: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpTool.process_llm_request` replaces the declaration with a fenced one, wrapping the description in `<<<BEGIN_UNTRUSTED_TOOL_DESCRIPTION>>>` / `<<<END_UNTRUSTED_TOOL_DESCRIPTION>>>` and adding a preamble about them to the system instruction. The source text is intact inside the markers.
notes_by_num.3: Koog 1.3.0-beta: the four tools that reach the model keep their descriptions unchanged. `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` leaves `deliver_payload` out of the registry (`DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser.parse` throws on its typeless `oneOf` and `fromClient` only logs it), so its description never reaches the model.

destructive-hint.title: `destructiveHint`
destructive-hint.description: An MCP tool annotation the author sets to declare that a tool is destructive, it deletes data, is irreversible, or has a large blast radius. It lives in the tool's `annotations` object alongside readOnlyHint, idempotentHint and openWorldHint.
destructive-hint.question: Is the destructive marker present at each capture boundary?
destructive-hint.notes: 2 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 10 changed or retained elsewhere, 19 dropped. A framework can keep the annotation outside the captured definition, in its own tool metadata, where an application policy layer can still read it. That counts as retained elsewhere.
destructive-hint.summary: A framework can keep the annotation outside the captured definition, in its own tool metadata, where an application policy layer can still read it. That counts as retained elsewhere.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools.build_tools` registers each tool as `Function(name, description, parameters=inputSchema)`; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are not carried, so `destructiveHint` reaches neither the model nor the agent.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `MCPTool` exposes the tool's name, description and input schema. The MCP `Tool` it wraps is kept only on the private `MCPTool._tool`, so the hint is in no public field and not in the function dict LiteLLM is handed.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench.list_tools` builds a `ToolSchema` of name, description and parameters and discards the MCP tool, so the hint is neither in the definition nor retained elsewhere.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI: the adapted tool object exposes no annotations field, so the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPToolResolver` builds each `MCPNativeTool` from the sanitized name, the description and an `args_schema` generated from `inputSchema`, so the MCP tool's annotations are not kept anywhere on it and the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: `Tool.from_mcp_tool` builds a `dspy.Tool` from the MCP tool's name, description and `inputSchema` properties only; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are on no `Tool` field and in no dict the LM is handed, so `destructiveHint` is lost.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: retained on `McpTool.raw_mcp_tool.annotations`; the `FunctionDeclaration` in the model's `LlmRequest` has no annotations field.
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` builds each `haystack.tools.Tool` from the tool's name, description and `inputSchema` only, so `annotations.destructiveHint` does not reach the tool definition.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain: retained on `StructuredTool.metadata`, but absent from the OpenAI-compatible dictionary produced by `convert_to_openai_tool`.
notes_by_num.10: LangChain: retained on `StructuredTool.metadata`, but absent from the OpenAI-compatible dictionary produced by `convert_to_openai_tool`.
notes_by_num.11: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `FunctionTool` keeps only name, description and the rebuilt `fn_schema`; the MCP tool's annotations are not kept anywhere on it, so the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.12: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: `load_tools` builds each `FunctionTool` from the MCP tool's name, description and inputSchema only. The annotations are neither in the function spec nor kept anywhere on the `FunctionTool`.
notes_by_num.13: OpenAI Agents SDK: `FunctionTool` keeps `_mcp_title` only; the behavioural hints are not carried.
notes_by_num.14: Pydantic AI: retained in `ToolDefinition.metadata['annotations']`; not part of `parameters_json_schema`.
notes_by_num.15: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `MCPPluginBase.load_tools` reads name, description and inputSchema only. No annotation is kept on the KernelFunction or sent to the model.
notes_by_num.16: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt builds each `MCPAdaptTool` from the name, description and `inputSchema` properties only, so the MCP tool's annotations are not kept anywhere on it and the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.17: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `createDynamicTool` builds the Genkit tool from the MCP tool's `name` (prefixed `<server>/`), `description` and `inputSchema` only, with `outputSchema: z.any()` and `metadata: { mcp: { _meta } }`; `annotations.destructiveHint` is not carried anywhere on the `ToolDefinition` the model receives.
notes_by_num.18: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the provider tool carries name, description and parameters only. `destructiveHint` is not kept anywhere: the runtime's permission request for `delete_account` names the tool's title and a `readOnly` flag, nothing else.
notes_by_num.19: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPTool` builds its `FunctionDeclaration` from name, description and the converted schemas only. The annotations are kept only on the TypeScript-private `mcpTool` field, which nothing on the model path reads.
notes_by_num.20: Mastra 2.2.0: retained on the tool action's `mcp.annotations`; not part of the id, description or inputSchema the agent is handed.
notes_by_num.21: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `mcpToFunctionTool` builds the `FunctionTool` from the MCP tool's name, description and inputSchema only. The `destructiveHint` annotation is not on the tool the model is handed and is not kept anywhere beside it.
notes_by_num.22: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): toolsFromDefinitions copies the server's destructiveHint onto the tool's app-side `metadata.annotations`, not into the description or inputSchema a provider adapter serializes. An app can read it; the model is not shown it.
notes_by_num.23: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `MCPAdapter.listTools` keeps the server's annotations on the tool's app-side `metadata.annotations`, but the function tool `convertToOpenAITool` builds for the provider carries name, description and parameters only, so the model never sees `destructiveHint`.
notes_by_num.24: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: MCP tool annotations reach `ToolSpecification.metadata()` only; the `ToolSpecification` AiServices hands the `ChatModel` carries name, description and parameters, so the model never sees `destructiveHint`.
notes_by_num.25: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `AbstractMcpTool.declaration` builds the `FunctionDeclaration` from the MCP tool's name, description, `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` only. `McpTool` keeps the MCP annotations beside it, through its public `annotations()`, so `destructiveHint` is retained in framework metadata but never reaches the model.
notes_by_num.26: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `destructiveHint` is dropped. `DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser` builds a `ToolDescriptor` (name, description, parameters) and `McpTool` keeps only the `Client`, that descriptor and a string metadata map, so `annotations` never reach the chat-completions request and are not kept anywhere in Koog.
notes_by_num.27: Spring AI 2.0.1: `SyncMcpToolCallbackProvider` builds a `ToolDefinition`, which holds only a name, a description and the input schema, so `destructiveHint` is dropped.
notes_by_num.28: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): `McpClientTool` passes the model only the MCP tool's name, description, `inputSchema` (as `JsonSchema`) and `outputSchema` (as `ReturnJsonSchema`). It keeps the MCP `Tool` it was built from as the public `ProtocolTool` property, so `destructiveHint` is retained in framework metadata but never reaches the model.
notes_by_num.29: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `convertTool` builds the `FunctionDeclaration` from the tool's name, description, `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` only, and `mcpTool` keeps no other field of the `*mcp.Tool`, so `annotations.destructiveHint` is gone after listing.

known_issues: A policy layer reading retained metadata in LangChain, Pydantic AI, or Mastra sees a value absent from the captured tool definition; those integration surfaces can disagree.
Because the annotation is absent rather than false, a consumer cannot distinguish "not destructive" from "never told".
destructive-hint.why: A guardrail that reads the tool definition at the capture boundary can only tell a destructive call from a safe one if the hint survives to that point. A framework that keeps the value in its own metadata still lets an application policy layer read it. This measurement does not claim what a later provider request contains.

format.title: `format`
format.description: A semantic format hint on a string parameter.
format.question: Is the format constraint present at each capture boundary?
format.notes: 24 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 2 changed or retained elsewhere, 5 dropped. A framework that rebuilds the input schema from its own model class can drop `format`, or keep it inside an optional wrapper while losing it from a union branch.
format.summary: A framework that rebuilds the input schema from its own model class can drop `format`, or keep it inside an optional wrapper while losing it from a union branch.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: `email` and `date-time` remain inside generated optional wrappers; `destination.anyOf[0].format: uri` is absent from the generated `args_schema`.
notes_by_num.2: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `convert_tools_to_openai_schema` emits the strict OpenAI function schema from the Pydantic `args_schema`. `owner_email`'s `format: email` and `destination.anyOf[0]`'s `format: uri` are moved into the description text (`... Format: email`) and dropped from the schema; `created_after`'s `date-time` survives inside its nullable wrapper.
notes_by_num.3: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `McpToolSpec` rebuilds each `inputSchema` as a Pydantic model (`create_model_from_json_schema`), and the model's JSON schema is what `ToolMetadata.to_openai_tool` hands the LLM. The field becomes a plain `str`, so every `format` (`email`, `date-time`, `uri`) is dropped.
notes_by_num.4: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): `format` is removed from the provider schema and appended to the parameter description as text, e.g. `{format: "email"}` on `owner_email` and `{format: "uri"}` inside the `destination` anyOf branch.
notes_by_num.5: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPTool._getDeclaration` passes `inputSchema` through `toGeminiSchema`, which keeps `type`, `description`, `enum`, `items`, `properties`, `required` and `anyOf` in the genai `Schema` dialect; `format` is not among them, so `owner_email` (`email`), `created_after` (`date-time`) and `destination.anyOf[0]` (`uri`) become plain strings.
notes_by_num.6: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpToolProvider` maps each `inputSchema` into LangChain4j's own `JsonSchemaElement` model (`JsonObjectSchema`, `JsonStringSchema`, `JsonIntegerSchema`, ...), and the `ToolSpecification` AiServices hands the `ChatModel` is built from that model. `JsonStringSchema` holds a description only, so every `format` (`email`, `date-time`, `uri`) is dropped.
notes_by_num.7: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `format` is dropped: `DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser` maps a string property to `ToolParameterType.String`, which has no format slot, so `owner_email` (email) and `created_after` (date-time) reach the model as plain strings. `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` leaves `deliver_payload` out of the registry (`DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser.parse` throws on its typeless `oneOf` and `fromClient` only logs it), so its `format: uri` is lost with the whole tool.

idempotent-hint.title: `idempotentHint`
idempotent-hint.description: Marks repeated calls as safe: calling twice has no additional effect.
idempotent-hint.question: Is the idempotentHint annotation present at each capture boundary?
idempotent-hint.notes: 2 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 10 changed or retained elsewhere, 19 dropped. A framework can keep the annotation outside the captured definition, in its own tool metadata, where an application policy layer can still read it. That counts as retained elsewhere.
idempotent-hint.summary: A framework can keep the annotation outside the captured definition, in its own tool metadata, where an application policy layer can still read it. That counts as retained elsewhere.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools.build_tools` registers each tool as `Function(name, description, parameters=inputSchema)`; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are not carried, so `idempotentHint` reaches neither the model nor the agent.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `MCPTool` exposes the tool's name, description and input schema. The MCP `Tool` it wraps is kept only on the private `MCPTool._tool`, so the hint is in no public field and not in the function dict LiteLLM is handed.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench.list_tools` discards the MCP tool after building the `ToolSchema`, so the hint is neither in the definition nor retained elsewhere.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI: the adapted tool object exposes no annotations field, so the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPToolResolver` builds each `MCPNativeTool` from the sanitized name, the description and an `args_schema` generated from `inputSchema`, so the MCP tool's annotations are not kept anywhere on it and the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: `Tool.from_mcp_tool` builds a `dspy.Tool` from the MCP tool's name, description and `inputSchema` properties only; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are on no `Tool` field and in no dict the LM is handed, so `idempotentHint` is lost.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: retained on `McpTool.raw_mcp_tool.annotations`; the `FunctionDeclaration` in the model's `LlmRequest` has no annotations field.
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` builds each `haystack.tools.Tool` from the tool's name, description and `inputSchema` only, so `annotations.idempotentHint` does not reach the tool definition.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain: retained on `StructuredTool.metadata`, but absent from the OpenAI-compatible dictionary produced by `convert_to_openai_tool`.
notes_by_num.10: LangChain: retained on `StructuredTool.metadata`, but absent from the OpenAI-compatible dictionary produced by `convert_to_openai_tool`.
notes_by_num.11: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `FunctionTool` keeps only name, description and the rebuilt `fn_schema`; the MCP tool's annotations are not kept anywhere on it, so the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.12: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: `load_tools` builds each `FunctionTool` from the MCP tool's name, description and inputSchema only. The annotations are neither in the function spec nor kept anywhere on the `FunctionTool`.
notes_by_num.13: OpenAI Agents SDK: `FunctionTool` keeps `_mcp_title` only. The behavioural hints are not carried.
notes_by_num.14: Pydantic AI: retained in `ToolDefinition.metadata['annotations']`. Not part of `parameters_json_schema`.
notes_by_num.15: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `MCPPluginBase.load_tools` reads name, description and inputSchema only. No annotation is kept on the KernelFunction or sent to the model.
notes_by_num.16: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt builds each `MCPAdaptTool` from the name, description and `inputSchema` properties only, so the MCP tool's annotations are not kept anywhere on it and the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.17: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `createDynamicTool` builds the Genkit tool from the MCP tool's `name` (prefixed `<server>/`), `description` and `inputSchema` only, with `outputSchema: z.any()` and `metadata: { mcp: { _meta } }`; `annotations.idempotentHint` is not carried anywhere on the `ToolDefinition` the model receives.
notes_by_num.18: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the provider tool carries name, description and parameters only, and the runtime's permission request names title and `readOnly`. `idempotentHint` is not kept anywhere.
notes_by_num.19: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPTool` builds its `FunctionDeclaration` from name, description and the converted schemas only. The annotations are kept only on the TypeScript-private `mcpTool` field, which nothing on the model path reads.
notes_by_num.20: Mastra 2.2.0: retained on the tool action's `mcp.annotations`; not part of the id, description or inputSchema the agent is handed.
notes_by_num.21: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `mcpToFunctionTool` builds the `FunctionTool` from the MCP tool's name, description and inputSchema only. The `idempotentHint` annotation is not on the tool the model is handed and is not kept anywhere beside it.
notes_by_num.22: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): toolsFromDefinitions copies the server's idempotentHint onto the tool's app-side `metadata.annotations`, not into the description or inputSchema a provider adapter serializes. An app can read it; the model is not shown it.
notes_by_num.23: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `MCPAdapter.listTools` keeps the server's annotations on the tool's app-side `metadata.annotations`, but the function tool `convertToOpenAITool` builds for the provider carries name, description and parameters only, so the model never sees `idempotentHint`.
notes_by_num.24: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: MCP tool annotations reach `ToolSpecification.metadata()` only; the `ToolSpecification` AiServices hands the `ChatModel` carries name, description and parameters, so the model never sees `idempotentHint`.
notes_by_num.25: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `AbstractMcpTool.declaration` builds the `FunctionDeclaration` from the MCP tool's name, description, `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` only. `McpTool` keeps the MCP annotations beside it, through its public `annotations()`, so `idempotentHint` is retained in framework metadata but never reaches the model.
notes_by_num.26: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `idempotentHint` is dropped. `DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser` builds a `ToolDescriptor` (name, description, parameters) and `McpTool` keeps only the `Client`, that descriptor and a string metadata map, so `annotations` never reach the chat-completions request and are not kept anywhere in Koog. `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` leaves `deliver_payload` out of the registry (`DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser.parse` throws on its typeless `oneOf` and `fromClient` only logs it), so its hint is lost with the whole tool.
notes_by_num.27: Spring AI 2.0.1: `SyncMcpToolCallbackProvider` builds a `ToolDefinition`, which holds only a name, a description and the input schema, so `idempotentHint` is dropped.
notes_by_num.28: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): `McpClientTool` passes the model only the MCP tool's name, description, `inputSchema` (as `JsonSchema`) and `outputSchema` (as `ReturnJsonSchema`). It keeps the MCP `Tool` it was built from as the public `ProtocolTool` property, so `idempotentHint` is retained in framework metadata but never reaches the model.
notes_by_num.29: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `convertTool` builds the `FunctionDeclaration` from the tool's name, description, `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` only, and `mcpTool` keeps no other field of the `*mcp.Tool`, so `annotations.idempotentHint` is gone after listing.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: nested types are re expressed via `$defs` and `$ref`. Semantically equivalent, so mcp-mirror resolves the reference before comparing rather than reporting it as flattening.
notes_by_num.2: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `McpToolSpec` rebuilds each `inputSchema` as a Pydantic model (`create_model_from_json_schema`), and the model's JSON schema is what `ToolMetadata.to_openai_tool` hands the LLM. null-acceptance.title: Null Acceptance
null-acceptance.description: Distinguishes an optional parameter that may be omitted from a parameter that explicitly accepts null.
null-acceptance.question: Does adaptation preserve whether each parameter accepts null?
null-acceptance.notes: 28 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 3 changed or retained elsewhere, 0 dropped. Wrapping an optional field in a union that accepts null changes the source nullability.
null-acceptance.summary: Wrapping an optional field in a union that accepts null changes the source nullability.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: optional fields are emitted through nullable anyOf wrappers, broadening the accepted values beyond omission alone.
notes_by_num.2: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `convert_tools_to_openai_schema` emits the strict OpenAI function schema from the Pydantic `args_schema`, which wraps each optional property in `anyOf: [..., {type: null}]`, so the model is offered `null` where the source only allowed omission. `MCPClient._clean_tool_arguments` then drops every `None` argument (and every dict left empty) before `tools/call`, so a null the model sends never reaches the server.
notes_by_num.3: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `McpToolSpec` rebuilds each `inputSchema` as a Pydantic model (`create_model_from_json_schema`), and the model's JSON schema is what `ToolMetadata.to_openai_tool` hands the LLM. Every optional field becomes `Optional[...] = None`, so its schema gains an `anyOf` branch of `null` the server never declared.

numeric-range.title: Numeric Ranges
numeric-range.question: Is the numeric range constraint present at each capture boundary?
numeric-range.notes: 26 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 0 changed or retained elsewhere, 5 dropped. A framework that rebuilds the input schema from its own model class can drop the bounds. Where a framework builds its schema from a model class, optional parameters are wrapped, and a constraint that stays inside the wrapper counts as present.
numeric-range.summary: A framework that rebuilds the input schema from its own model class can drop the bounds. Where a framework builds its schema from a model class, optional parameters are wrapped, and a constraint that stays inside the wrapper counts as present.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: preserved inside the `anyOf` wrapper emitted for optional fields, so the constraint sits one level down rather than being lost.
notes_by_num.2: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `McpToolSpec` rebuilds each `inputSchema` as a Pydantic model (`create_model_from_json_schema`), and the model's JSON schema is what `ToolMetadata.to_openai_tool` hands the LLM. Fields become plain `int`/`float` with no constraints, so `minimum` and `maximum` are dropped.
notes_by_num.3: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): `minimum` and `maximum` are removed from the provider schema and appended to the parameter description as text, e.g. `{minimum: 1, maximum: 100}` on `limit`.
notes_by_num.4: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPTool._getDeclaration` passes `inputSchema` through `toGeminiSchema`, which keeps `type`, `description`, `enum`, `items`, `properties`, `required` and `anyOf` in the genai `Schema` dialect; `minimum` and `maximum` are not among them, so `limit`'s bounds and `max_words.minimum` are dropped.
notes_by_num.5: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpToolProvider` maps each `inputSchema` into LangChain4j's own `JsonSchemaElement` model (`JsonObjectSchema`, `JsonStringSchema`, `JsonIntegerSchema`, ...), and the `ToolSpecification` AiServices hands the `ChatModel` is built from that model. `JsonIntegerSchema` and `JsonNumberSchema` hold a description only, so `minimum` and `maximum` are dropped.
notes_by_num.6: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `minimum` and `maximum` are dropped: `ToolParameterType.Integer` has no range slot, so `limit` (1 to 100) and `max_words` reach the model as bare integers.

one-of-any-of.title: `oneOf` / `anyOf`
one-of-any-of.description: A parameter that accepts one of several shapes, using JSON Schema 2020-12 combinators.
one-of-any-of.question: Do both union combinators survive to each capture boundary?
one-of-any-of.notes: 24 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 6 changed or retained elsewhere, 1 dropped. A framework that regenerates the schema can preserve `anyOf` while collapsing `oneOf`.
one-of-any-of.summary: A framework that regenerates the schema can preserve `anyOf` while collapsing `oneOf`.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: `destination.anyOf` survives, while `mode.oneOf` is collapsed by the generated `args_schema`; the combined capability is therefore only partly preserved.
notes_by_num.2: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `convert_tools_to_openai_schema` emits the strict OpenAI function schema from the Pydantic `args_schema`, which rewrites `mode.oneOf` as an `anyOf` of `const` branches plus `null`. `destination.anyOf` survives as `anyOf`.
notes_by_num.3: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `McpToolSpec` rebuilds each `inputSchema` as a Pydantic model (`create_model_from_json_schema`), and the model's JSON schema is what `ToolMetadata.to_openai_tool` hands the LLM. A `oneOf` becomes the `anyOf` of a Pydantic union, and an object branch loses its properties.
notes_by_num.4: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.models.get_tool_json_schema` rewrites an `anyOf` as a list of its branches' `type`s, so `destination` becomes `type: ["string", "object"]` and the object branch loses its properties. `mode.oneOf` survives, with `type: "string"` added beside it.
notes_by_num.5: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPTool._getDeclaration` passes `inputSchema` through `toGeminiSchema`, which keeps `type`, `description`, `enum`, `items`, `properties`, `required` and `anyOf` in the genai `Schema` dialect. `anyOf` survives, but `oneOf` has no case: `deliver_payload.mode` arrives as `type: TYPE_UNSPECIFIED` with its description and no branches.
notes_by_num.6: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpToolProvider` maps each `inputSchema` into LangChain4j's own `JsonSchemaElement` model (`JsonObjectSchema`, `JsonStringSchema`, `JsonIntegerSchema`, ...), and the `ToolSpecification` AiServices hands the `ChatModel` is built from that model. `anyOf` maps to `JsonAnyOfSchema` and survives. The model has no `oneOf`, so `deliver_payload.mode` becomes an empty `{"type": "object", "properties": {}}` and its alternatives are lost.
notes_by_num.7: Koog 1.3.0-beta: no `anyOf` or `oneOf` reaches the model. The fixture's only `anyOf`/`oneOf` tool is `deliver_payload`, and `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` leaves it out of the registry: `DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser.parse` throws `IllegalArgumentException: Parameter Delivery mode. must have type property.` on its typeless `oneOf`, and `fromClient` only logs it.

open-world-hint.title: `openWorldHint`
open-world-hint.description: Marks a tool as touching the open world: external, non deterministic effects.
open-world-hint.question: Is the openWorldHint annotation present at each capture boundary?
open-world-hint.notes: 2 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 10 changed or retained elsewhere, 19 dropped. A framework can keep the annotation outside the captured definition, in its own tool metadata, where an application policy layer can still read it. That counts as retained elsewhere.
open-world-hint.summary: A framework can keep the annotation outside the captured definition, in its own tool metadata, where an application policy layer can still read it. That counts as retained elsewhere.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools.build_tools` registers each tool as `Function(name, description, parameters=inputSchema)`; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are not carried, so `openWorldHint` reaches neither the model nor the agent.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `MCPTool` exposes the tool's name, description and input schema. The MCP `Tool` it wraps is kept only on the private `MCPTool._tool`, so the hint is in no public field and not in the function dict LiteLLM is handed.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench.list_tools` discards the MCP tool after building the `ToolSchema`, so the hint is neither in the definition nor retained elsewhere.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI: the adapted tool object exposes no annotations field, so the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPToolResolver` builds each `MCPNativeTool` from the sanitized name, the description and an `args_schema` generated from `inputSchema`, so the MCP tool's annotations are not kept anywhere on it and the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: `Tool.from_mcp_tool` builds a `dspy.Tool` from the MCP tool's name, description and `inputSchema` properties only; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are on no `Tool` field and in no dict the LM is handed, so `openWorldHint` is lost.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: retained on `McpTool.raw_mcp_tool.annotations`; the `FunctionDeclaration` in the model's `LlmRequest` has no annotations field.
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` builds each `haystack.tools.Tool` from the tool's name, description and `inputSchema` only, so `annotations.openWorldHint` does not reach the tool definition.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain: retained on `StructuredTool.metadata`, but absent from the OpenAI-compatible dictionary produced by `convert_to_openai_tool`.
notes_by_num.10: LangChain: retained on `StructuredTool.metadata`, but absent from the OpenAI-compatible dictionary produced by `convert_to_openai_tool`.
notes_by_num.11: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `FunctionTool` keeps only name, description and the rebuilt `fn_schema`; the MCP tool's annotations are not kept anywhere on it, so the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.12: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: `load_tools` builds each `FunctionTool` from the MCP tool's name, description and inputSchema only. The annotations are neither in the function spec nor kept anywhere on the `FunctionTool`.
notes_by_num.13: OpenAI Agents SDK: `FunctionTool` keeps `_mcp_title` only. The behavioural hints are not carried.
notes_by_num.14: Pydantic AI: retained in `ToolDefinition.metadata['annotations']`. Not part of `parameters_json_schema`.
notes_by_num.15: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `MCPPluginBase.load_tools` reads name, description and inputSchema only. No annotation is kept on the KernelFunction or sent to the model.
notes_by_num.16: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt builds each `MCPAdaptTool` from the name, description and `inputSchema` properties only, so the MCP tool's annotations are not kept anywhere on it and the value is not recoverable after adaptation.
notes_by_num.17: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `createDynamicTool` builds the Genkit tool from the MCP tool's `name` (prefixed `<server>/`), `description` and `inputSchema` only, with `outputSchema: z.any()` and `metadata: { mcp: { _meta } }`; `annotations.openWorldHint` is not carried anywhere on the `ToolDefinition` the model receives.
notes_by_num.18: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the provider tool carries name, description and parameters only, and the runtime's permission request names title and `readOnly`. `openWorldHint` is not kept anywhere.
notes_by_num.19: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPTool` builds its `FunctionDeclaration` from name, description and the converted schemas only. The annotations are kept only on the TypeScript-private `mcpTool` field, which nothing on the model path reads.
notes_by_num.20: Mastra 2.2.0: retained on the tool action's `mcp.annotations`; not part of the id, description or inputSchema the agent is handed.
notes_by_num.21: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `mcpToFunctionTool` builds the `FunctionTool` from the MCP tool's name, description and inputSchema only. The `openWorldHint` annotation is not on the tool the model is handed and is not kept anywhere beside it.
notes_by_num.22: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): toolsFromDefinitions copies the server's openWorldHint onto the tool's app-side `metadata.annotations`, not into the description or inputSchema a provider adapter serializes. An app can read it; the model is not shown it.
notes_by_num.23: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `MCPAdapter.listTools` keeps the server's annotations on the tool's app-side `metadata.annotations`, but the function tool `convertToOpenAITool` builds for the provider carries name, description and parameters only, so the model never sees `openWorldHint`.
notes_by_num.24: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: MCP tool annotations reach `ToolSpecification.metadata()` only; the `ToolSpecification` AiServices hands the `ChatModel` carries name, description and parameters, so the model never sees `openWorldHint`.
notes_by_num.25: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `AbstractMcpTool.declaration` builds the `FunctionDeclaration` from the MCP tool's name, description, `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` only. `McpTool` keeps the MCP annotations beside it, through its public `annotations()`, so `openWorldHint` is retained in framework metadata but never reaches the model.
notes_by_num.26: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `openWorldHint` is dropped. `DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser` builds a `ToolDescriptor` (name, description, parameters) and `McpTool` keeps only the `Client`, that descriptor and a string metadata map, so `annotations` never reach the chat-completions request and are not kept anywhere in Koog.
notes_by_num.27: Spring AI 2.0.1: `SyncMcpToolCallbackProvider` builds a `ToolDefinition`, which holds only a name, a description and the input schema, so `openWorldHint` is dropped.
notes_by_num.28: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): `McpClientTool` passes the model only the MCP tool's name, description, `inputSchema` (as `JsonSchema`) and `outputSchema` (as `ReturnJsonSchema`). It keeps the MCP `Tool` it was built from as the public `ProtocolTool` property, so `openWorldHint` is retained in framework metadata but never reaches the model.
notes_by_num.29: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `convertTool` builds the `FunctionDeclaration` from the tool's name, description, `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` only, and `mcpTool` keeps no other field of the `*mcp.Tool`, so `annotations.openWorldHint` is gone after listing.

property-descriptions.description: Natural-language guidance attached to individual parameters and nested properties.
property-descriptions.question: Do property-level descriptions survive at each capture boundary?
property-descriptions.notes: 27 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 4 changed or retained elsewhere, 0 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI: descriptions on the URI and object branches of destination.anyOf are absent from the generated args_schema.
notes_by_num.2: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `convert_tools_to_openai_schema` emits the strict OpenAI function schema from the Pydantic `args_schema`. The descriptions on both `destination.anyOf` branches and on the `create_report.config` object are absent from the generated schema; the other descriptions survive, with allowed values and ranges appended to them.
notes_by_num.3: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `McpToolSpec` rebuilds each `inputSchema` as a Pydantic model (`create_model_from_json_schema`), and the model's JSON schema is what `ToolMetadata.to_openai_tool` hands the LLM. Property descriptions survive at the top level, but descriptions on the branches of an `anyOf` are dropped.
notes_by_num.4: Koog 1.3.0-beta: the four tools that reach the model keep their property descriptions. `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` leaves `deliver_payload` out of the registry (`DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser.parse` throws on its typeless `oneOf` and `fromClient` only logs it), so its four property descriptions never reach the model.

required.title: `required`
required.description: Which parameters must be supplied for the call to be valid.
required.question: Is the required parameter set present at each capture boundary?
required.notes: 25 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 6 changed or retained elsewhere, 0 dropped. Where a framework builds its schema from a model class, optional parameters are wrapped, and a constraint that stays inside the wrapper counts as present.
required.summary: Where a framework builds its schema from a model class, optional parameters are wrapped, and a constraint that stays inside the wrapper counts as present.

notes_by_num.1: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: the strict tool schema (`use_strict_tool_schema=True`, the ChatModel default) marks every property required at every level. `create_report` gains `sections`, `config.include_summary` and each section's `body`, and the optional properties are not made nullable, so the model must invent values for them.
notes_by_num.2: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `convert_tools_to_openai_schema` emits the strict OpenAI function schema from the Pydantic `args_schema`, which lists every property in `required` and expresses optional ones as nullable `anyOf` wrappers, so the source `required` lists are rewritten on every object.
notes_by_num.3: DSPy 3.4.0: `Tool.format_as_litellm_function_call` recomputes `required` as every property without a `default`, so optional parameters become required (for example `deliver_payload.mode` and `create_report.status`). `from_mcp_tool` reads the server's `required` only to append " (Required)" to `arg_desc`, which is not in the dict. `dspy.ReAct` prints `str(tool)` with no required list at all.
notes_by_num.4: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `McpToolSpec` rebuilds each `inputSchema` as a Pydantic model (`create_model_from_json_schema`), and the model's JSON schema is what `ToolMetadata.to_openai_tool` hands the LLM. Top-level `required` survives, but the `required` list of every nested object is lost with its properties.
notes_by_num.5: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt hands smolagents only `inputSchema.properties`, so the source `required` list is lost, and `smolagents.models.get_tool_json_schema` rebuilds `required` from every property not marked `nullable`. Every optional parameter becomes required (`explain_topic.max_words`, `search_records.limit`), and smolagents rejects a call that omits one before it reaches the server.
notes_by_num.6: Koog 1.3.0-beta: top-level `required` survives, nested `required` does not. The `ToolDescriptor` keeps it (`config` has `requiredProperties = [format]`, `sections.items` has `[heading]`), but the schema `OpenAILLMClient` serializes for the request leaves `required` off nested objects and array items. `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` leaves `deliver_payload` out of the registry (`DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser.parse` throws on its typeless `oneOf` and `fromClient` only logs it), so its `required` lists are lost with the whole tool.

tool-icons.title: `icons`
tool-icons.description: An optional array of display icons on a tool definition, each with a source URL, MIME type and size list.
tool-icons.question: Does the tool's icon set reach the agent's tool definition?
tool-icons.notes: 1 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 4 changed or retained elsewhere, 26 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools.build_tools` registers each tool as `Function(name, description, parameters=inputSchema)`; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are not carried, so `icons` are discarded.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `icons` is dropped; the MCP `Tool` survives only on the private `MCPTool._tool`.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: `ToolSchema` has no icon field and `McpWorkbench` keeps no copy of the MCP tool.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI: `crewai_tools` contains no reference to `icons` anywhere in the package, so the field has nowhere to survive adaptation.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient._list_tools_impl` keeps only the name, description and `inputSchema` of each tool, and neither `MCPNativeTool` nor the OpenAI function schema has an icon field, so the icons are not kept.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: `Tool.from_mcp_tool` builds a `dspy.Tool` from the MCP tool's name, description and `inputSchema` properties only; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are on no `Tool` field and in no dict the LM is handed, so `icons` are discarded.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: retained on `McpTool.raw_mcp_tool.icons`; `FunctionDeclaration` has no icon field.
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` builds each `haystack.tools.Tool` from the tool's name, description and `inputSchema` only, so `icons` does not reach the tool definition.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain: `langchain_mcp_adapters` contains no reference to `icons`. `StructuredTool.metadata` carries annotations but no icon set.
notes_by_num.10: LangChain: `langchain_mcp_adapters` contains no reference to `icons`. `StructuredTool.metadata` carries annotations but no icon set.
notes_by_num.11: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `FunctionTool` and `ToolMetadata` have no icon field, and the icons are not kept.
notes_by_num.12: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: `FunctionTool` has no icon field and `load_tools` does not read `icons`.
notes_by_num.13: OpenAI Agents SDK: the `agents` package contains no reference to `icons`. `FunctionTool` keeps `_mcp_title` only.
notes_by_num.14: Pydantic AI: `pydantic_ai.mcp` declares `icons: list[Icon] | None` on its resource type only. `ToolDefinition` has no icon field, so tool icons are dropped.
notes_by_num.15: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: icons are not read by `load_tools` and are not kept on the KernelFunction.
notes_by_num.16: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt builds each `MCPAdaptTool` from the name, description and `inputSchema` properties only, and neither `smolagents.Tool` nor the function-tool dict has an icon field, so the icons are not kept.
notes_by_num.17: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPAgentTool.tool_spec` builds the `ToolSpec` from name, description, schemas and annotations. Icons stay on `MCPAgentTool.mcp_tool.icons` and never reach the spec the model receives.
notes_by_num.18: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `createDynamicTool` builds the Genkit tool from the MCP tool's `name` (prefixed `<server>/`), `description` and `inputSchema` only, with `outputSchema: z.any()` and `metadata: { mcp: { _meta } }`; `icons` does not survive.
notes_by_num.19: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): `icons` are not carried onto the provider tool or kept anywhere the session exposes.
notes_by_num.20: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `FunctionDeclaration` has no icon field, and `MCPTool` keeps the icons only on its TypeScript-private `mcpTool` field.
notes_by_num.21: Mastra 2.2.0: `@mastra/mcp` types `icons` under resource and configuration shapes. No tool type carries it, and the tool action's `mcp` metadata holds annotations only.
notes_by_num.22: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `mcpToFunctionTool` builds the `FunctionTool` from the MCP tool's name, description and inputSchema only. The tool's `icons` list is not on the tool the model is handed and is not kept anywhere beside it.
notes_by_num.23: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): toolsFromDefinitions reads name, title, description, inputSchema, annotations and _meta from each listed tool. `icons` is not copied onto the tool object, so it is dropped.
notes_by_num.24: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `icons` is not carried onto the `DynamicStructuredTool` or its metadata, so neither the provider tool nor the application can read it.
notes_by_num.25: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: tool `icons` reach `ToolSpecification.metadata()` only, so they never reach the `ChatModel`.
notes_by_num.26: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `McpTool` keeps the MCP tool's annotations and `_meta`, not its `icons`; the `FunctionDeclaration` has no place for them.
notes_by_num.27: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `icons` are dropped. The `ToolDescriptor` has no icon field and `McpTool` does not keep the SDK `Tool`.
notes_by_num.28: Spring AI 2.0.1: `SyncMcpToolCallbackProvider` builds a `ToolDefinition`, which holds only a name, a description and the input schema, so `icons` is dropped.
notes_by_num.29: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): `icons` stay on the public `McpClientTool.ProtocolTool` (framework metadata); the `AIFunction` the model is given has no place for them.
notes_by_num.30: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `convertTool` builds the `FunctionDeclaration` from the tool's name, description, `inputSchema` and `outputSchema` only, and `mcpTool` keeps no other field of the `*mcp.Tool`, so `icons` is gone after listing.

tool-name.title: `name`
tool-name.description: The identifier a downstream consumer uses to invoke the tool.
tool-name.question: Is the tool name unchanged at each capture boundary?
tool-name.notes: 25 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 6 changed or retained elsewhere, 0 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPToolResolver` names a stdio tool `<command>_<args joined by _>_<tool>` and an HTTP or SSE tool `<host>_<port>_<path>_<tool>`, passed through `sanitize_tool_name`, and `MCPServerStdio`/`MCPServerHTTP`/`MCPServerSSE` have no name or prefix option. Measured with the relative launch `python fixtures/tricky_server.py`, `search_records` becomes `python_fixtures_tricky_server_py_search_records`. When the prefix pushes a name past 64 characters it is truncated and an 8-character hash appended, so an absolute launch path can hide the MCP tool name entirely.
notes_by_num.2: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: the OpenAI request names each function `<plugin>-<tool>` (here `mcp-search_records`), the kernel's fully qualified name. The MCP name survives after the prefix.
notes_by_num.3: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): tools reach the model as `<server>-<tool>`, here `src-search_records`. The prefix is the key the host gives the server in `SessionConfig.mcpServers`.
notes_by_num.4: Mastra 2.2.0: captured tool actions are namespaced as `<serverKey>_<toolName>`, so `delete_account` becomes `src_delete_account`.
notes_by_num.5: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `MCPAdapter` names every tool `<server>_<tool>` (one underscore since 2.0.1, two before), so the model sees `src_search_records` for the server's `search_records`. The prefix is the server key in `servers` and is on by default; the per-server `prefixToolNameWithServerName: false` option, which was not measured, removes it.
notes_by_num.6: Koog 1.3.0-beta: names pass through unchanged, but `deliver_payload` never reaches the model. `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` catches any `Throwable` from `DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser.parse` and only logs it, so a tool it cannot parse is left out of the `ToolRegistry`. Its `mode` property is a `oneOf` of `const`s with no `type`, and the parser throws `IllegalArgumentException: Parameter Delivery mode. must have type property.` (the message uses the property's description where its name belongs). Only a log line records the loss.

verdict.headline: Mixed across the 31 frameworks that reach 2025-11-25.
verdict.detail: Prefixing is a transformation rather than a loss, but it changes the exact invocation identifier.

tool-name.usage_note: Not published. Candidate source: count of public MCP servers using this capability. Not estimated, so the panel stays empty until the corpus is scanned.
known_issues: A prefixed name changes between server configurations, so a hard coded allowlist can silently stop matching.
tool-name.why: Name based routing, allowlists, and eval fixtures that match exact tool names break under prefixing.

content-annotations.title: Content `annotations`
content-annotations.description: The `audience`, `priority` and `lastModified` hints that content blocks, resources and prompt messages may carry.
content-annotations.question: Do content annotations survive to the agent?
content-annotations.notes: 0 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 12 changed or retained elsewhere, 19 dropped. Annotations say who a block is for and how much it matters.
content-annotations.summary: Annotations say who a block is for and how much it matters.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` keeps each block's text or media only; content annotations (`audience`, `priority`) are dropped at both boundaries.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: block annotations survive on the content objects `MCPTool.run` returns, but not next to `structuredContent`, and the tool message carries them only inside the serialized JSON string (agent: `n`).
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: Boundary-dependent. `McpWorkbench.call_tool` and the `AssistantAgent` path keep only the text of a block, dropping `annotations`; the `mcp_server_tools` adapter's `run_json` returns the MCP content blocks with their annotations.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI: every content block is dropped, annotations with them.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient._call_tool_impl` keeps only `content[0]`, returning its `text` when it has one and `str(content[0])` otherwise, and a text block is returned as its bare `text`, so a block's `annotations` are gone at `BaseTool.run` and in the agent's tool message.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: text blocks come back as plain `str`, so block `annotations` are dropped at both the direct and the ReAct boundary.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: block annotations are intact in the tool's return value. At the model they are only keys inside the JSON `FunctionResponse.response`; no content block carries them.
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): boundary-dependent. The direct `Tool.invoke` return is that JSON string, which the adapter's docstring says to read with `json.loads`; parsed, it keeps every block. embedded-resource-content.title: Embedded resources
embedded-resource-content.description: A tool result block that inlines a resource's contents together with its URI and MIME type.
embedded-resource-content.question: Does an embedded resource keep its identity, or arrive as anonymous text?
embedded-resource-content.notes: 0 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 22 changed or retained elsewhere, 9 dropped. An embedded resource carries its own identity: a uri, a mime type, and contents.
embedded-resource-content.summary: An embedded resource carries its own identity: a uri, a mime type, and contents.

notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: Boundary-dependent. `McpWorkbench.call_tool` raises `Unknown content type from server` on a `ResourceLink` and returns that message as an error result (so does the agent path); `mcp_server_tools`' `run_json` returns the `ResourceLink` block.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26: returned on its own, the resource link comes back as the stringified content model, so its `uri`, name and description survive only as characters. Beside other content kinds it is dropped and only the text reaches the agent.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient._call_tool_impl` keeps only `content[0]`, returning its `text` when it has one and `str(content[0])` otherwise. Returned on its own, the resource link comes back as the stringified content model ({shape}), so {kept} survive only as characters, at `BaseTool.run` and in the tool message the agent loop builds. Beside other content kinds it is dropped and only the leading text reaches the agent.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: with the default `result_mode="text"`, `Tool.acall` returns the resource link block as the MCP content object when the result has no text (direct: `y`). In a `dspy.ReAct` run the observation the model reads is that object's Python repr, `«name='linked.txt' uri='file:///fixtures/linked.txt' ...»` (react: `a`). When a result carries any text block, `_convert_mcp_tool_result` returns the text alone and drops the resource link block at both boundaries.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: the tool's return value (`after_tool_callback`) is the dumped `CallToolResult`, with this block intact in `content`. The model receives that dict as `FunctionResponse.response`, a JSON value: the block survives as JSON text, and no media is lifted into `FunctionResponse.parts`.
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): boundary-dependent. The direct `Tool.invoke` return is that JSON string, which the adapter's docstring says to read with `json.loads`; parsed, it keeps every block. The `ChatMessage` an `Agent` hands the next generator turn carries the Tool's return value as one text: the `CallToolResult` JSON from `model_dump_json`. The resource link arrives as JSON inside that text, not as a link block.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain: at both result boundaries the link becomes a LangChain `file` content block carrying the uri as `url` and the `mime_type`. The link's name and description are gone.
notes_by_num.10: LangChain: at both result boundaries the link becomes a LangChain `file` content block carrying the uri as `url` and the `mime_type`. The link's name and description are gone.
notes_by_num.11: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `FunctionTool._parse_tool_output` has no case for `CallToolResult`, so the `ToolOutput`, and the `ChatMessage(role="tool")` a `FunctionAgent` sends the model, hold one text block: the result's Python repr. The link survives only as characters inside that repr.
notes_by_num.12: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: a lone resource link becomes a `uri` `Content` carrying uri and media type; its name and description are dropped. Beside `structuredContent` it is replaced by the structured JSON.
notes_by_num.13: OpenAI Agents: serialized into a text block holding the link's JSON, so name, uri and description survive as characters rather than as fields.
notes_by_num.14: Pydantic AI: reduced to a bare text block containing only the uri. The link's name and description are gone.
notes_by_num.15: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `_mcp_content_types_to_kernel_content` passes the link's `AnyUrl` to `BinaryContent(uri=...)`, which rejects it, so any result containing a resource link raises and the whole call fails. The model is told only that the function failed.
notes_by_num.16: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `MCPAdaptTool.forward` handles text, image and audio only and raises `ValueError: ... returned an unsupported content type` for a resource link, which a `ToolCallingAgent` turns into an `Error:` message. Beside other content kinds it is dropped, because `MCPAdaptTool.forward` reads only `content[0]` and logs a warning when there are more.
notes_by_num.17: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `map_mcp_content_to_tool_result_content` handles text, image and embedded-resource blocks only. A `resource_link` block is dropped with a debug log, alone or beside other blocks.
notes_by_num.18: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `processResult` returns `{ error }` for `isError`, `structuredContent` when the server sent one, the joined text (JSON-parsed when it looks like JSON) when every block is text, the lone block when there is one, and otherwise the whole `CallToolResult`. A lone resource link is returned as the block itself, so it survives; in `mixed_content` the server also sent `structuredContent`, which is returned alone, and the link is gone.
notes_by_num.19: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): depends on the boundary. `agent`: the `tool` message the provider receives is an empty string; the link's `uri`, `name` and `description` are dropped. `direct`: `session.rpc.tools.execute` returns the `resource_link` block whole.
notes_by_num.20: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: boundary-dependent. `MCPTool.runAsync` returns the `CallToolResult` unchanged (`afterToolCallback` sees it with every block intact), and ADK puts that object in the `functionResponse` of the next `LlmRequest`. At `direct` the resource_link block is intact. At `agent` it survives only as JSON inside `functionResponse.response`; no `fileData` part is built.
notes_by_num.21: Mastra 2.2.0: a result without `structuredContent` comes back unchanged, resource_link intact with its name, uri, description and mimeType. When the result carries `structuredContent`, that value is returned in place of the whole result and the link is gone.
notes_by_num.22: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the model receives a resource link as its JSON serialization inside a text item; `MCPServer.callTool` itself returns the block intact.
notes_by_num.23: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient.callTool` keeps the `resource_link` block. `toLlmContent` turns it into the text `name: uri`, so its description and mimeType do not reach the model.
notes_by_num.24: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): execute resolves with the CallToolResult, so a caller reading a step's toolResults gets the resource link block intact. The adapter's toModelOutput converter maps only text and image blocks, so the model receives a resource link block as a text part holding the block's JSON (the uri, name and MIME type as characters). Boundary-dependent: kept at execute, flattened to text at model_output.
notes_by_num.25: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): a `resource_link` becomes a LangChain `file` block with `url`, `mimeType` and `metadata.{uri,name}`; its `description` is kept only in the app-side artifact.
notes_by_num.26: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: The default `McpToolExecutor` result converter accepts text blocks only. Any `resource_link` block makes it throw `Unsupported content type: "resource_link"`: the direct executor raises it as a `RuntimeException`, and AiServices turns it into an error tool result the model reads in place of the block. A result with `structuredContent` never reads its blocks at all.
notes_by_num.27: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `AbstractMcpTool.wrapCallResult` turns a result that holds any block other than text into `{"error": "Tool '<name>' returned content that is not TextContent.", "content_details": ...}` when no text block is present, and drops the non-text blocks when one is (`mixed_content` returns only the text). Both boundaries see the same map.
notes_by_num.28: Koog 1.3.0-beta: boundary-dependent. At `direct` the resource link keeps its uri, name and mimeType. `AIAgent` sends the tool's result to the model as one `role: tool` message whose content is `McpTool.encodeResultToString`: the JSON of the whole `CallToolResult` (`content`, `isError`, `structuredContent`), or `Error: <text>` when `isError` is set. At `agent` the link is JSON text inside that message.
notes_by_num.29: Spring AI 2.0.1: the tool result reaches the agent and a direct `ToolCallback.call` as one string: the JSON of the result's content list with each block's `type` field dropped, e.g. `[{"name":"linked.txt","uri":"file:///fixtures/linked.txt",...}]`. The link survives only as JSON text, with nothing marking it as a link.
notes_by_num.30: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): `McpClientTool` has no `AIContent` for a `resource_link`, so it returns the whole `CallToolResult` as a JSON string at both boundaries. The link's fields are readable only by parsing that text.
notes_by_num.31: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcpTool.Run` returns `{"output": text}`, where `formatMCPContent` replaces the block with a placeholder line (`[MCP resource link: uri=..., mimeType=..., name=..., description=...]`), and the model receives that map as `FunctionResponse.response`. When the result also has `structuredContent`, as in the mixed result, `Run` returns `{"output": structuredContent}` and the block is dropped.

structured-content.title: `structuredContent`
structured-content.description: A JSON result value returned alongside `content`, conforming to the tool's `outputSchema` when one is declared.
structured-content.question: Does the agent receive the structured value, or only its text rendering?
structured-content.notes: 8 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 9 changed or retained elsewhere, 14 dropped. structuredContent is the typed value; the text content beside it is a mirror meant for humans. An adapter that hands the agent only the mirror drops the typed value.
structured-content.summary: structuredContent is the typed value; the text content beside it is a mirror meant for humans. An adapter that hands the agent only the mirror drops the typed value.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: boundary-dependent. The `ToolResult` the Function entrypoint returns keeps `structuredContent` in `metadata['structured_content']`; the tool `Message` the next model turn receives carries the text content only, so the model never gets the structured value.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: when a result has `structuredContent`, `MCPTool._run` returns it alone and drops every content block (direct: `y`). The model gets `JSONToolOutput.get_text_content()`, the structured value serialized as one JSON string with no separate field (agent: `n`).
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: Every boundary drops `structuredContent`: `ToolResult` holds text and image parts only, and `McpToolAdapter.run_json` returns `result.content` alone.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI: structuredContent is dropped; only the text mirror reaches the agent.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient._call_tool_impl` keeps only `content[0]`, returning its `text` when it has one and `str(content[0])` otherwise and never reads `structuredContent`, so only the text mirror reaches the agent.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: with the default `result_mode="text"`, `_convert_mcp_tool_result` returns the text blocks only, so `structuredContent` reaches neither the caller nor a `dspy.ReAct` observation. The documented non-default `from_mcp_tool(..., result_mode="structured")` returns `structuredContent` alone and drops the text.
notes_by_num.7: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): boundary-dependent. The direct `Tool.invoke` return is that JSON string, which the adapter's docstring says to read with `json.loads`; parsed, it keeps every block. The `ChatMessage` an `Agent` hands the next generator turn carries the Tool's return value as one text: the `CallToolResult` JSON from `model_dump_json`. `structuredContent` appears in that text, never as a structured value.
notes_by_num.8: LangChain: structuredContent is dropped; only the text mirror reaches the agent.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain: structuredContent is dropped; only the text mirror reaches the agent.
notes_by_num.10: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `FunctionTool._parse_tool_output` has no case for `CallToolResult`, so the `ToolOutput`, and the `ChatMessage(role="tool")` a `FunctionAgent` sends the model, hold one text block: the result's Python repr. `structuredContent` appears in that text, never as a structured value.
notes_by_num.11: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: with the default `tool_result_content="structured_first"` the adapter serializes `structuredContent` to JSON and returns it as one text `Content` in place of the content blocks. No structured value reaches the agent; the complete CallToolResult rides in the function result's `additional_properties` for hosts, which a chat client does not send.
notes_by_num.12: OpenAI Agents: structuredContent is dropped; only the text mirror reaches the agent.
notes_by_num.13: Pydantic AI: `structuredContent` is returned only when every content part is text, and then in place of the text. A result that also carries an image or audio block loses the typed value and passes only the text mirror.
notes_by_num.14: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `_mcp_call_tool_result_to_kernel_contents` converts `content` only; `structuredContent` is discarded at both boundaries.
notes_by_num.15: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): with `structured_output` left at its default (`False`, the legacy behavior; smolagents warns the default will change), `MCPAdaptTool.forward` returns `content[0]` and never reads `structuredContent`, so only the text mirror reaches the agent. `MCPClient(..., structured_output=True)` returns `structuredContent` instead; that opt-in was not measured.
notes_by_num.16: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): depends on the boundary. `agent`: `structuredContent` is serialised as JSON and appended to the text in the `tool` message (`SENTINEL_TEXT_BLOCK\n\n{"count":2,...}`); no structured value reaches the provider. `direct`: `session.rpc.tools.execute` returns `structuredContent` as an object.
notes_by_num.17: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `MCPServer.callTool` keeps `structuredContent` on the returned array, but the model never receives it by default: the agent hands over the content blocks. With the non-default `useStructuredContent: true` it hands over `JSON.stringify(structuredContent)` as text instead, which is not the typed value either.
notes_by_num.18: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient.callTool` returns `structuredContent`. `toLlmContent` uses it only when the result has no content blocks, as JSON text, so a result with text and structured content reaches the model without the typed value.
notes_by_num.19: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): execute resolves with the CallToolResult including structuredContent. toModelOutput maps only the `content` list, so the model gets the text blocks and never the typed value. Boundary-dependent: kept at execute, dropped at model_output. With a caller-supplied outputSchema (the `schemas` option), execute returns the validated structuredContent instead; that path was not measured.
notes_by_num.20: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): the tool is `content_and_artifact`. `structuredContent` goes into the artifact as `mcp_structured_content`, which LangChain keeps app-side; the `ToolMessage` content the model reads, and the `tool.invoke` value, hold only the text mirror.
notes_by_num.21: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: when a result has `structuredContent`, `McpToolExecutor` returns it as `ToolExecutionResult.result()` and sets `resultText` to its Jackson re-serialization. The direct executor therefore yields the structured value (direct: `y`), while the agent's `ToolExecutionResultMessage` carries only that JSON string (agent: `n`).
notes_by_num.22: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `wrapCallResult` reads only `CallToolResult.content()`; `structuredContent` is dropped. `text_and_structured` returns `{"text_output": [{"text": "SENTINEL_TEXT_BLOCK"}]}` at both boundaries.
notes_by_num.23: Spring AI 2.0.1: `structuredContent` is dropped at both boundaries; the agent and a direct `ToolCallback.call` see only the JSON of the content list.

tool-audio-content.title: Audio content
tool-audio-content.description: The `audio` content block, carrying base64-encoded audio data and its MIME type.
tool-audio-content.question: Does an audio result survive adaptation?
tool-audio-content.notes: 3 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 22 changed or retained elsewhere, 6 dropped. An adapter that raises on a block it cannot convert, instead of degrading it, loses the rest of the result with it.
tool-audio-content.summary: An adapter that raises on a block it cannot convert, instead of degrading it, loses the rest of the result with it.

notes_by_num.1: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `MCPTool.run` returns the `AudioContent` object (direct: `y`), but drops it next to `structuredContent`. The model gets it as one JSON string with the base64 data inline, not as audio (agent: `a`).

notes_by_num.3: CrewAI 1.15.26: returned on its own, the audio comes back as the stringified content model with its base64 data and `audio/wav` MIME type as characters. Beside other content kinds it is dropped and only the text reaches the agent.

Returned on its own, the audio comes back as the stringified content model ({shape}), so {kept} survive only as characters, at `BaseTool.run` and in the tool message the agent loop builds. Beside other content kinds it is dropped and only the leading text reaches the agent.

notes_by_num.6: Google ADK 2.11.0: the tool's return value (`after_tool_callback`) is the dumped `CallToolResult`, with this block intact in `content`. notes_by_num.7: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): boundary-dependent. The direct `Tool.invoke` return is that JSON string, which the adapter's docstring says to read with `json.loads`; parsed, it keeps every block. The `ChatMessage` an `Agent` hands the next generator turn carries the Tool's return value as one text: the `CallToolResult` JSON from `model_dump_json`. notes_by_num.12: OpenAI Agents: the block is serialized into a text block containing its JSON, base64 payload and all, so the audio reaches the agent only as characters.
notes_by_num.13: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: boundary-dependent. `Kernel.invoke` returns AudioContent. The model's tool message is the Python repr of that object; no audio part is sent.

notes_by_num.25: Koog 1.3.0-beta: boundary-dependent. At `direct` the audio block keeps its data and mimeType. `AIAgent` sends the tool's result to the model as one `role: tool` message whose content is `McpTool.encodeResultToString`: the JSON of the whole `CallToolResult` (`content`, `isError`, `structuredContent`), or `Error: <text>` when `isError` is set. notes_by_num.26: Spring AI 2.0.1: the tool result reaches the agent and a direct `ToolCallback.call` as one string: the JSON of the result's content list with each block's `type` field dropped, e.g. `[{"data":"UklGR...","mimeType":"audio/wav"}]`. The base64 survives as characters in a string, with nothing marking it as audio.
notes_by_num.27: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): a lone audio block becomes a `DataContent` with its bytes and MIME type at both boundaries. Beside `structuredContent` (`mixed_content`) `McpClientTool` returns the `CallToolResult` as JSON, so the audio reaches the model as base64 characters inside a text result, not as audio.
notes_by_num.28: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcpTool.Run` returns `{"output": text}`, where `formatMCPContent` replaces the block with a placeholder line (`[MCP audio: mimeType="audio/wav", size=44 bytes]`, with no audio data), and the model receives that map as `FunctionResponse.response`. When the result also has `structuredContent`, as in the mixed result, `Run` returns `{"output": structuredContent}` and the block is dropped.
