tool-execution-errors.title: `isError`
tool-execution-errors.description: The in-band flag marking a tool result as a tool execution error, which the spec expects clients to pass to the model so it can correct itself.
tool-execution-errors.question: Can the agent tell a tool execution error from a successful result?
tool-execution-errors.notes: 7 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 18 changed or retained elsewhere, 6 dropped. Measured at the value a direct invocation returns and at the value the framework's own agent path returns. Where those disagree, the cell is marked as boundary-dependent rather than dropped.
tool-execution-errors.summary: Measured at the value a direct invocation returns and at the value the framework's own agent path returns. Where those disagree, the cell is marked as boundary-dependent rather than dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: an `isError` result becomes the text `Error from MCP tool '<name>': <repr of the content list>` with no error flag: the `ToolResult` has none, and the tool `Message` the model receives has `tool_call_error=False`, which is set only when the call raises.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: depends on the boundary. `MCPTool._run` raises `ToolError` with the result JSON for an `isError` result, so the error survives only as an exception (direct: `a`). A `RequirementAgent` writes it through its tool_error template, "The tool has failed; the error log is shown below...", into the tool message (agent: `y`).
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: Boundary-dependent. `McpWorkbench.call_tool` and the agent's `FunctionExecutionResult` carry `is_error`; `McpToolAdapter.run_json` raises an `Exception` holding the serialized content instead of returning a flagged result.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI: the adapter's tool reads only `result.content` and never `result.isError`, so a failed call returns the same bare string a successful one does. Identical at `BaseTool.run` and at `CrewStructuredTool.invoke`, which is the path a crew run takes.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): depends on the boundary. `MCPNativeTool._run_async` reads `isError` and returns a `ToolFailure(reason=mcp_error)` carrying the error text, so a direct `BaseTool.run` caller can tell a failure from a result (direct: `y`). In an agent run, `execute_single_native_tool_call` renders only the failure's message into the tool message, so the model gets the bare error text with no error flag, the same shape as a successful result (agent: `n`).
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: depends on the boundary. `Tool.acall` raises `RuntimeError("Failed to call a MCP tool: ...")` for an `isError` result, so the error survives only as an exception (direct: `a`). `dspy.ReAct` catches it and hands the model the text `Execution error in tool_error:` followed by a Python traceback, with no error flag (react: `n`). The traceback also carries the host's file paths into the prompt.
notes_by_num.7: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): boundary-dependent. For an `isError` result `MCPClient.call_tool` raises `MCPInvocationError`, which `Tool.invoke` wraps in `ToolInvocationError`, so a direct caller gets an exception rather than the result. An `Agent` catches it and hands the next generator turn a tool `ChatMessage` with the error text and `error=True`.
notes_by_num.8: LangChain: the answer depends on the boundary. `load_mcp_tools` builds the tool with `handle_tool_error=_handle_mcp_tool_error`, so an `isError` result raises an internal `ToolException` subclass that the handler turns back into tool output. Invoked with a plain argument dict the call returns those content blocks and nothing marks them as a failure. Invoked with a `ToolCall`, which is what an agent and `ToolNode` send, the same call returns a `ToolMessage` with `status="error"`.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain: the answer depends on the boundary. `load_mcp_tools` builds the tool with `handle_tool_error=_handle_mcp_tool_error`, so an `isError` result raises an internal `ToolException` subclass that the handler turns back into tool output. Invoked with a plain argument dict the call returns those content blocks and nothing marks them as a failure. Invoked with a `ToolCall`, which is what an agent and `ToolNode` send, the same call returns a `ToolMessage` with `status="error"`.
notes_by_num.10: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `FunctionTool._parse_tool_output` has no case for `CallToolResult`, so the `ToolOutput`, and the `ChatMessage(role="tool")` a `FunctionAgent` sends the model, hold one text block: the result's Python repr. `ToolOutput.is_error` is set only when the call raises, and an `isError` result does not raise, so it is `False`; the tool message the `FunctionAgent` builds carries no error field at all. `isError=True` survives only as characters in the text.
notes_by_num.11: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: an `isError` result makes `MCPTool.call_tool` raise `ToolExecutionException` with the server's text. On the agent path the function-invocation loop turns that into a function result reading `Error: Function failed.`; the server's message reaches the model only with `include_detailed_errors=True`.
notes_by_num.12: OpenAI Agents: `invoke_mcp_tool` reads `isError` only to decide whether `structuredContent` may be preferred, then emits the error text as an ordinary text output item. Identical at `MCPUtil.invoke_mcp_tool` and at `FunctionTool.on_invoke_tool`, which is what the agent loop calls. By default nothing reaching app code carries the flag either: the `on_tool_end` hook gets the same text item a success produces. Opt-in: an `MCPServer` built with `custom_data_extractor` is handed `is_error`, and whatever it returns is attached to the run's `ToolCallOutputItem.custom_data`; the model and the hook still get the unflagged text.
notes_by_num.13: Pydantic AI: the toolset's `tool_error_behavior` defaults to `'retry'`, which raises `ModelRetry` carrying the error text. Identical at `direct_call_tool` and at `call_tool`, which delegates to it; an agent run records that raise as a typed `RetryPromptPart` rather than as a tool return.
notes_by_num.14: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `call_tool` ignores `isError`, so a failed tool returns its text as an ordinary result, and the model reads it with no error signal.
notes_by_num.15: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `MCPAdaptTool.forward` never reads `result.isError`, so a failed call returns the same bare string a successful one does, and a `ToolCallingAgent` sends it to the model as an ordinary `Observation:`. Only a raised exception becomes an `Error:` message.
notes_by_num.16: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): depends on the boundary. `agent`: the server's text reaches the provider as `MCP server 'src': SENTINEL_TOOL_ERROR: ...` in an ordinary `tool` message, with no error flag. `direct`: `session.rpc.tools.execute` returns `resultType: "failure"` with the same text.
notes_by_num.17: Mastra 2.2.0: the per-server `onToolError` option defaults to `'throw'`, so the tool action throws a `MastraError` carrying the error text. Set to `'return'` the same action resolves with the server's `CallToolResult`, `isError: true` included.
notes_by_num.18: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: depends on the boundary. `MCPServer.callTool` returns the content array with `isError` attached to it, so a direct caller can read the flag. The `function_call_result` the model receives has no error field: a failed call arrives as ordinary text, the same shape as a success.
notes_by_num.19: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient.callTool` returns `isError: true` to a direct caller. `toLlmContent` returns only the content blocks, so the model gets the failure text with no error flag; the README's agent-tool example carries `isError` beside it in user code.
notes_by_num.20: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): an isError result is not thrown. execute resolves with the CallToolResult, isError: true, which a caller reading a step's toolResults can see. generateText then builds the model's message through toModelOutput, which keeps only the content, so the model receives the error text as an ordinary tool result with no failure flag; ai's createToolModelOutput uses its error-text path only for a tool that threw. Boundary-dependent: flagged at execute, unflagged at model_output.
notes_by_num.21: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): boundary-dependent. Inside a LangGraph `ToolNode` the failure reaches the model as a `ToolMessage` with `status: "error"` and the server's text. A direct `tool.invoke` throws a `ToolException` carrying the text instead of returning a result.
notes_by_num.22: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: an `isError` result reaches the agent as a `ToolExecutionResultMessage` with `isError` set and the error text intact (agent: `y`). The direct executor throws `McpApplicationErrorException`, an LLM-visible `ToolExecutionException`, with that text instead of returning a result (direct: `a`).
notes_by_num.23: Spring AI 2.0.1: boundary-dependent. On the agent path (`DefaultToolCallingManager.executeToolCalls`) an `isError` result reaches the model as the text `Error calling tool: [TextContent[annotations=null, text=...]]`, a Java record's toString, with no error flag. A direct `ToolCallback.call` throws `ToolExecutionException` carrying that same message.
notes_by_num.24: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): depends on the boundary. `direct`: `mcpTool.Run` turns an `isError` result into the Go error `Tool execution failed. Details: <text>`, so the caller gets an `error`, not a result. `agent`: ADK hands the model `{"error": "Tool execution failed. Details: SENTINEL_TOOL_ERROR: ..."}` as the `FunctionResponse`, so the model sees the failure and the server's text.

tool-execution-errors.why: MCP separates protocol errors from tool execution errors precisely so a model can retry the second kind with better arguments. A framework that raises both as exceptions, or reports both as success, collapses that distinction and removes the recovery path the spec designed.

tool-image-content.title: Image content
tool-image-content.description: The `image` content block, carrying base64-encoded data and its MIME type.
tool-image-content.question: Does an image result survive adaptation, or is it dropped or flattened to text?
tool-image-content.notes: 10 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 19 changed or retained elsewhere, 2 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `MCPTool.run` returns the `ImageContent` object (direct: `y`), but drops it next to `structuredContent`. The model gets it as one JSON string with the base64 data inline, not as an image (agent: `a`).
notes_by_num.2: AutoGen 0.7.5: Boundary-dependent. `McpWorkbench.call_tool` returns an `ImageResultContent` (a decoded PIL image, MIME type gone), but the `AssistantAgent` hands the model `ToolResult.to_text()`, where the image is the text `[Image: <base64>]`. In a mixed result the workbench raises on the audio block and drops everything.
notes_by_num.3: CrewAI 1.15.26: returned on its own, the image comes back as the stringified content model, `type='image' data='...' mimeType='image/png'`, so the bytes and MIME type survive only as characters. Beside other content kinds it is dropped and only the text reaches the agent.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient._call_tool_impl` keeps only `content[0]`, returning its `text` when it has one and `str(content[0])` otherwise. Returned on its own, the image comes back as the stringified content model ({shape}), so {kept} survive only as characters, at `BaseTool.run` and in the tool message the agent loop builds. Beside other content kinds it is dropped and only the leading text reaches the agent.
notes_by_num.5: DSPy 3.4.0: with the default `result_mode="text"`, `Tool.acall` returns the image block as the MCP content object when the result has no text (direct: `y`). In a `dspy.ReAct` run the observation the model reads is that object's Python repr, `«type='image' data='...' mime_type='image/png' ...»` (react: `a`). When a result carries any text block, `_convert_mcp_tool_result` returns the text alone and drops the image block at both boundaries.
notes_by_num.6: Google ADK 2.11.0: the tool's return value (`after_tool_callback`) is the dumped `CallToolResult`, with this block intact in `content`. The model receives that dict as `FunctionResponse.response`, a JSON value: the block survives as JSON text, and no media is lifted into `FunctionResponse.parts`.
notes_by_num.7: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): boundary-dependent. The direct `Tool.invoke` return is that JSON string, which the adapter's docstring says to read with `json.loads`; parsed, it keeps every block. The `ChatMessage` an `Agent` hands the next generator turn carries the Tool's return value as one text: the `CallToolResult` JSON from `model_dump_json`. The image arrives as base64 inside that text, not as an image block.
notes_by_num.8: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `FunctionTool._parse_tool_output` has no case for `CallToolResult`, so the `ToolOutput`, and the `ChatMessage(role="tool")` a `FunctionAgent` sends the model, hold one text block: the result's Python repr. The image survives only as characters (`ImageContent(type='image', data='...', mime_type='image/png')`); the model gets no image part.
notes_by_num.9: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: a lone image becomes a `data` `Content` with a data URI and media type, which a provider client can send as an image. Beside `structuredContent` it is dropped, because the default `tool_result_content="structured_first"` hands the model only the structured JSON.
notes_by_num.10: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: boundary-dependent. `Kernel.invoke` returns ImageContent. The model's tool message is the Python repr of that object, with the base64 inside a string; no image part is sent.
notes_by_num.11: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): depends on the boundary. Called directly, the tool returns a `PIL.Image` decoded from the image block, so the image survives. In a `ToolCallingAgent` run the image is stored in agent memory and the next model turn carries only the text `Observation:\nStored 'image.png' in memory.`, with no image part. Beside other content kinds it is dropped at both, because `MCPAdaptTool.forward` reads only `content[0]` and logs a warning when there are more.
notes_by_num.12: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `processResult` returns `{ error }` for `isError`, `structuredContent` when the server sent one, the joined text (JSON-parsed when it looks like JSON) when every block is text, the lone block when there is one, and otherwise the whole `CallToolResult`. A lone image block is returned as the block itself, so it survives; in `mixed_content` the server also sent `structuredContent`, which is returned alone, and the image is gone. With `createMcpHost({ multipart: true })`, a non-default option, images become `media` parts beside the output.
notes_by_num.13: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: boundary-dependent. `MCPTool.runAsync` returns the `CallToolResult` unchanged (`afterToolCallback` sees it with every block intact), and ADK puts that object in the `functionResponse` of the next `LlmRequest`. At `direct` the image block keeps its data and mimeType. At `agent` it is a JSON value inside `functionResponse.response`, and no media is lifted into an `inlineData` part, so the model gets no image.
notes_by_num.14: Mastra 2.2.0: a result without `structuredContent` comes back unchanged, image block intact with its data and mimeType. When the result carries `structuredContent`, that value is returned in place of the whole result and the image is gone.
notes_by_num.15: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: a lone image block reaches the model as an `input_image` item. When a result has several blocks the SDK stringifies the whole content array into one text item, so an image beside other kinds arrives as JSON text.
notes_by_num.16: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: The default `McpToolExecutor` result converter accepts text blocks only. Any `image` block makes it throw `Unsupported content type: "image"`: the direct executor raises it as a `RuntimeException`, and AiServices turns it into an error tool result the model reads in place of the block. A result with `structuredContent` never reads its blocks at all.
notes_by_num.17: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `AbstractMcpTool.wrapCallResult` turns a result that holds any block other than text into `{"error": "Tool '<name>' returned content that is not TextContent.", "content_details": ...}` when no text block is present, and drops the non-text blocks when one is (`mixed_content` returns only the text). Both boundaries see the same map.
notes_by_num.18: Koog 1.3.0-beta: boundary-dependent. At `direct` the image block keeps its data and mimeType. `AIAgent` sends the tool's result to the model as one `role: tool` message whose content is `McpTool.encodeResultToString`: the JSON of the whole `CallToolResult` (`content`, `isError`, `structuredContent`), or `Error: <text>` when `isError` is set. At `agent` the base64 data is a string inside that JSON; no image part reaches the model.
notes_by_num.19: Spring AI 2.0.1: the tool result reaches the agent and a direct `ToolCallback.call` as one string: the JSON of the result's content list with each block's `type` field dropped, e.g. `[{"data":"iVBOR...","mimeType":"image/png"}]`. The base64 survives as characters in a string; no image reaches a chat model as an image.
notes_by_num.20: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): a lone image block becomes a `DataContent` with its bytes and MIME type at both boundaries. Beside `structuredContent` (`mixed_content`) `McpClientTool` returns the `CallToolResult` as JSON, so the image reaches the model as base64 characters inside a text result, not as an image.
notes_by_num.21: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcpTool.Run` returns `{"output": text}`, where `formatMCPContent` replaces the block with a placeholder line (`[MCP image: mimeType="image/png", size=70 bytes]`, with no image data), and the model receives that map as `FunctionResponse.response`. When the result also has `structuredContent`, as in the mixed result, `Run` returns `{"output": structuredContent}` and the block is dropped.

tool-output-schema.title: `outputSchema`
tool-output-schema.description: An optional JSON Schema on the tool definition describing the shape of the tool's structured result.
tool-output-schema.question: Does the output schema survive to the agent's tool definition?
tool-output-schema.notes: 6 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 5 changed or retained elsewhere, 20 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools.build_tools` registers each tool as `Function(name, description, parameters=inputSchema)`; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are not carried, so `outputSchema` is discarded; no output contract reaches the model.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `outputSchema` is dropped; the MCP `Tool` survives only on the private `MCPTool._tool`, and `JSONToolOutput` is not validated against it.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: `ToolSchema` has no output schema field and `McpWorkbench` keeps no copy of `outputSchema`.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26: neither `crewai_tools` nor `crewai` reads an MCP tool's `outputSchema`, so the adapted tool has none.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient._list_tools_impl` keeps only the name, description and `inputSchema` of each tool, so `outputSchema` is gone before the tool is built.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: `Tool.from_mcp_tool` builds a `dspy.Tool` from the MCP tool's name, description and `inputSchema` properties only; the tool's annotations, title, icons and `outputSchema` are on no `Tool` field and in no dict the LM is handed, so `outputSchema` is discarded.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: with JSON_SCHEMA_FOR_FUNC_DECL on, the default, `McpTool._get_declaration` sends the MCP `outputSchema` to the model as `FunctionDeclaration.response_json_schema`. Every keyword survives; the top-level description is wrapped in `<<<BEGIN_UNTRUSTED_TOOL_DESCRIPTION>>>` fences (data/measurements/scan/google_adk.json).
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` builds each `haystack.tools.Tool` from the tool's name, description and `inputSchema` only, so `outputSchema` does not reach the tool definition.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain: `langchain_mcp_adapters` 0.3.2 contains no reference to `outputSchema`. `StructuredTool` keeps the input schema and, in `metadata`, the annotations.
notes_by_num.10: LangChain: `langchain_mcp_adapters` 0.3.2 contains no reference to `outputSchema`. `StructuredTool` keeps the input schema and, in `metadata`, the annotations.
notes_by_num.11: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `ToolMetadata` carries `fn_schema` for input only; the MCP `outputSchema` is not kept and never reaches the model.
notes_by_num.12: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: `load_tools` reads only the inputSchema; the tool's `outputSchema` is not on the `FunctionTool` or in `to_json_schema_spec()`.
notes_by_num.13: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: the `agents` package never reads a tool's `outputSchema`; `FunctionTool` carries an input schema only.
notes_by_num.14: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: `MCPToolset.get_tools` copies `outputSchema` onto `ToolDefinition.return_schema`, but the definition is sent to a model without it unless `include_return_schema=True` or the `IncludeToolReturnSchemas` capability is set. Neither is the default.
notes_by_num.15: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `load_tools` ignores `outputSchema`; the KernelFunction declares no return schema and the request carries none.
notes_by_num.16: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): with `structured_output` left at its default (`False`), mcpadapt does not read the MCP tool's `outputSchema`, and the function-tool dict smolagents builds has no output field, so it never reaches the model. `structured_output=True` resolves it onto the tool; that opt-in was not measured.
notes_by_num.17: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: the MCP `outputSchema` is dropped: `createDynamicTool` declares `outputSchema: z.any()`, so the `ToolDefinition` carries `{"$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#"}` in its place, a schema that accepts anything.
notes_by_num.18: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): `outputSchema` is not on the provider tool and is not kept anywhere the session exposes.
notes_by_num.19: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `_getDeclaration` converts `outputSchema` with `toGeminiSchema` and sends it as the declaration's `response` schema, so it reaches the model in the genai dialect, minus what that drops (`count.minimum` on the fixture).
notes_by_num.20: Mastra 2.2.0: the tool action declares `outputSchema` beside `inputSchema`, every keyword intact with a `$schema` dialect (JSON Schema 2020-12) added, and checks `structuredContent` against it.
notes_by_num.21: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `mcpToFunctionTool` builds the `FunctionTool` from the MCP tool's name, description and inputSchema only. The tool's `outputSchema` is not on the tool the model is handed and is not kept anywhere beside it.
notes_by_num.22: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): in the default `schemas: "automatic"` mode, `mcpClient.tools()` builds each tool with `dynamicTool` from the MCP `inputSchema` only, so the server's `outputSchema` is on neither the tool the model is handed nor anything beside it. An `outputSchema` is used only when the application passes its own `schemas` entry for the tool.
notes_by_num.23: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `outputSchema` is used only to validate a modern in-band elicitation round; it is not on the `DynamicStructuredTool`, its metadata or the provider tool.
notes_by_num.24: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `outputSchema` reaches `ToolSpecification.metadata()` only; the model is never shown it.
notes_by_num.25: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `outputSchema` is dropped. The `ToolDescriptor` describes inputs only, and the chat-completions function has no output schema field.
notes_by_num.26: Spring AI 2.0.1: `SyncMcpToolCallbackProvider` builds a `ToolDefinition`, which holds only a name, a description and the input schema, so `outputSchema` is dropped.

tool-text-content.title: Text content
tool-text-content.description: The `text` content block, the baseline result type that every tool result may carry.
tool-text-content.question: Does text content reach the agent unchanged?
tool-text-content.notes: 17 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 14 changed or retained elsewhere, 0 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: a text block survives on its own, but next to `structuredContent` it is dropped: `MCPTool._run` returns the structured value alone. The model gets the block as the JSON of the `TextContent` object, wrapper keys included, not its bare text.
notes_by_num.2: AutoGen 0.7.5: Text survives at every boundary on its own, but a result that also carries an audio or resource-link block makes `McpWorkbench.call_tool` raise, so the text in that result reaches the agent only as the error message.
notes_by_num.3: CrewAI: the text arrives stringified inside a Python list repr, as "['SENTINEL_TEXT_BLOCK']" rather than the block's text.
notes_by_num.4: Google ADK 2.11.0: the tool's return value keeps each text block in `content`. The model receives the whole dumped `CallToolResult` as `FunctionResponse.response`, so the text arrives wrapped in JSON rather than as plain text.
notes_by_num.5: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: text beside media blocks arrives as a plain string, byte-identical. When every content part is text and the result carries `structuredContent`, the typed value is returned in place of the text, so the text block is gone.
notes_by_num.6: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: boundary-dependent. `Kernel.invoke` returns a TextContent per block. The model's tool message is `str()` of that list, the Python repr of SK's content objects, so the text is inside a repr string.
notes_by_num.7: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `processResult` returns `{ error }` for `isError`, `structuredContent` when the server sent one, the joined text (JSON-parsed when it looks like JSON) when every block is text, the lone block when there is one, and otherwise the whole `CallToolResult`. A text block reaches the model as text at every boundary, but beside `structuredContent` (`mixed_content`) only the structured value is returned and the text block is gone.
notes_by_num.8: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: boundary-dependent. `MCPTool.runAsync` returns the `CallToolResult` unchanged (`afterToolCallback` sees it with every block intact), and ADK puts that object in the `functionResponse` of the next `LlmRequest`. At `direct` the text block is a text block. At `agent` the model reads it inside one JSON object, `{"content": [{"type": "text", "text": ...}], ...}`, never as a plain text part.
notes_by_num.9: Mastra 2.2.0: a result without `structuredContent` comes back unchanged, text block intact. When the result carries `structuredContent`, that value is returned in place of the whole result, so every content block, text included, is gone.
notes_by_num.10: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: a text-only result reaches both boundaries unchanged. When the result also carries `structuredContent`, the executor returns the structured value's JSON in place of the text blocks, so the server's own text is lost (direct `mixed_content` and `text_and_structured`: `n`).
notes_by_num.11: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `AbstractMcpTool.wrapCallResult` returns `{"text_output": [...]}`, with each text block parsed as JSON or wrapped as `{"text": ...}`. The model's `functionResponse` and the `afterToolCallback` both see that map, so the text survives but not as plain text.
notes_by_num.12: Koog 1.3.0-beta: boundary-dependent. At `direct` (`EventHandler.onToolCallCompleted`) the `CallToolResult` is intact. `AIAgent` sends the tool's result to the model as one `role: tool` message whose content is `McpTool.encodeResultToString`: the JSON of the whole `CallToolResult` (`content`, `isError`, `structuredContent`), or `Error: <text>` when `isError` is set. At `agent` the text arrives inside that JSON, for example `{"content": [{"text": "SENTINEL_TEXT_BLOCK", "type": "text"}], "isError": false}`, not as bare text.
notes_by_num.13: Spring AI 2.0.1: the tool result reaches the agent and a direct `ToolCallback.call` as one string: the JSON of the result's content list with each block's `type` field dropped, e.g. `[{"text":"SENTINEL_TEXT_BLOCK"}]`. The text survives inside that JSON, not as a text block.
notes_by_num.14: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): a plain text result reaches the model intact as `{"output": text}`. When the result also has `structuredContent`, `mcpTool.Run` returns `{"output": structuredContent}` alone and the text blocks are dropped.

tools-list-changed.title: `notifications/tools/list_changed`
tools-list-changed.description: The notification a server sends when its tool list changes, delivered on a subscription stream the client opted into with `toolsListChanged`.
tools-list-changed.question: Does the framework refresh its tool list when the server says it changed?
tools-list-changed.notes: 13 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 11 changed or retained elsewhere, 7 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` registers no message handler, so no hook hears the notification. `build_tools` lists again, so the next build shows the change, but an `Agent` calls it per run only with `refresh_connection=True`.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no notification hook and no relist. Calling `MCPTool.from_client` again on the same session shows the change, so the caller has to know when to.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: The workbench registers no message handler, so no hook hears the notification; its `list_tools` asks the server every time, so the next listing shows the change.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` takes no message handler or callback, and its `tools` property returns the list it built at start. After the fixture added a tool and fired the notification, a crew was still handed the old list.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` with no message handler and has no list-changed hook, and `Agent(mcps=...)` resolves the tool list once, so `notifications/tools/list_changed` goes unseen and the agent keeps the stale list.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy has no notification hook and no relist. The change shows only when the caller lists again on its session and converts each tool with `from_mcp_tool` again.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` takes no message handler, so nothing an application registers hears the notification. `get_tools` relists on every call by default (`tool_list_cache_ttl_seconds=None`), so the next list showed the added tool anyway. ADK documents that with `tool_list_cache_ttl_seconds` set, a change goes unnoticed until the cache entry expires.
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` with no message handler, and `MCPToolset.warm_up` lists tools once and returns early after that, so `notifications/tools/list_changed` reaches nothing and the toolset keeps its first list.
notes_by_num.9: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` takes no message handler and closes its session after every call (over stdio it also starts a fresh server process per call), so no session is open to hear `notifications/tools/list_changed`, and the next `McpToolSpec` listing did not show the added tool.
notes_by_num.10: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: the default `message_handler` awaits `load_tools()` inside the MCP session's receive loop. Its `tools/list` reply cannot be read until the request times out (30 s here, never with the default `request_timeout=None`), so the call that triggered the change fails and the list stays stale.
notes_by_num.11: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt opens its `ClientSession` with no message handler, and `MCPClient.get_tools()` returns the list built at connect and never relists. After the fixture added a tool and fired the notification, the agent was still handed the old list.
notes_by_num.12: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: no handler for `notifications/tools/list_changed` is registered and there is no change hook; each `getActiveTools` call lists again, so a caller that re-lists sees the added tool.
notes_by_num.13: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPToolset` opens a new session for every operation (`getTools`, `listResources`, `readResource`, each tool call) and closes it after; over stdio that is a new server process each time. No session outlives the call that changed the list, and over stdio the added tool dies with its process, so the next `getTools` matched the one before.
notes_by_num.14: Mastra 2.2.0 against a 2025-11-25 server: `onListChanged('src', fn)` installs the handler, and it fired and the next list showed the change. But the call itself rejects with `subscriptions/listen needs MCP 2026-07-28`, because it also tries to open a 2026-07-28 stream. Code that awaits the registration sees an error for a hook that works.
notes_by_num.15: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the SDK takes no notification handler, so `notifications/tools/list_changed` reaches nothing. `cacheToolsList` defaults to false, so the next `listTools` (and the next agent turn) asks the server again and shows the change.
notes_by_num.16: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): MCPClient registers no notification handler: a server notification reaches only `onUncaughtError`, as an "Unsupported message type" error that does not name the notification. `client.tools()` lists again on every call, so the next call shows the added tool.
notes_by_num.17: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: The adapter registers no `toolsChangeConsumer` consumer, so nothing tells the agent the list changed. The next `McpToolset.getTools` call (or session `listTools`) lists again and shows the change.
notes_by_num.18: Koog 1.3.0-beta: `fromClient` lists tools once into a fixed `ToolRegistry` and registers no `notifications/tools/list_changed` handler, so the agent keeps the stale list. A new `fromClient` call on the same `Client` would list again.

resource-binary-contents.title: `blob` contents
resource-binary-contents.description: The base64 `blob` form of resource contents, used for anything that is not text.
resource-binary-contents.question: Can the agent read a binary resource without corrupting it?
resource-binary-contents.notes: 21 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 0 changed or retained elsewhere, 10 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so no resource contents, text or binary, reach the agent.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `beeai_framework.tools.mcp` has `MCPTool` only. `MCPTool.from_client` lists and wraps tools, and BeeAI has no MCP resource or prompt API.
notes_by_num.3: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` exposes only `tools`. It has no resource or prompt API, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient` has `list_tools`, `call_tool`, `list_prompts` and `get_prompt` and no resource API, and `Agent(mcps=...)` turns only the tools into `BaseTool`s, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes_by_num.5: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy's MCP support is `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`, which converts one tool. It has no resource or prompt API, so resources and prompts stay on the caller's MCP session.
notes_by_num.6: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` wraps tools as Haystack `Tool`s and has no resource or prompt API, and the `ClientSession` it opens is private to `MCPToolset._worker._client`, so binary resource contents are never read.
notes_by_num.7: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: `MCPTool` has no resource or resource-template API; `resources/list`, `resources/read` and `resources/templates/list` are never sent. (`MCPSkillsSource` reads resources, but only `skill://index.json` and the skills it names.)
notes_by_num.8: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `MCPPluginBase` loads tools and prompts only; it has no resource API.
notes_by_num.9: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` exposes only `get_tools()`, and the `ClientSession` lives on the private `MCPClient._adapter`. It has no resource or prompt API, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes_by_num.10: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `ReadResource` on.

resource-subscriptions.title: `notifications/resources/updated`
resource-subscriptions.description: Per-resource change notifications, opted into by listing URIs in a `subscriptions/listen` request and delivered as `notifications/resources/updated`.
resource-subscriptions.question: Can the agent watch a single resource for changes?
resource-subscriptions.notes: 2 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 12 changed or retained elsewhere, 17 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` has no subscribe method. Through the raw `ClientSession` at `MCPTools.session.session`, `subscribe_resource` is accepted, but no `notifications/resources/updated` reaches the caller.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: BeeAI has no subscribe API. Subscribing through the caller's `ClientSession` works on the wire, but BeeAI has no hook, so no update reaches the caller.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench` has no subscribe method and its `ClientSession` is private to `McpSessionActor`.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` exposes only `tools`; there is no subscribe route and no hook for `notifications/resources/updated`.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient` has `list_tools`, `call_tool`, `list_prompts` and `get_prompt` and no resource API, and `Agent(mcps=...)` turns only the tools into `BaseTool`s, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy has no subscribe API. Through `subscribe_resource` on the caller's `mcp.Client.session` the subscription is accepted, but no `notifications/resources/updated` reaches the caller.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` has no subscribe API. On the raw `ClientSession` from `MCPSessionManager.create_session()`, `subscribe_resource` / `unsubscribe_resource` worked and the server sent `notifications/resources/updated`, but ADK builds that session with no `message_handler` and offers no parameter for one, so the update reached no caller.
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` wraps tools as Haystack `Tool`s and has no resource or prompt API, and the `ClientSession` it opens is private to `MCPToolset._worker._client`, so there is no route to `resources/subscribe` and no handler for `notifications/resources/updated`.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2 has no subscribe API. The `ClientSession` that `create_session` yields is the raw SDK session, so `subscribe_resource` / `unsubscribe_resource` on it worked, and the update reached the `message_handler` passed through `session_kwargs`. That route belongs to the SDK, not the adapter.
notes_by_num.10: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2 has no subscribe API. The `ClientSession` that `create_session` yields is the raw SDK session, so `subscribe_resource` / `unsubscribe_resource` on it worked, and the update reached the `message_handler` passed through `session_kwargs`. That route belongs to the SDK, not the adapter.
notes_by_num.11: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` has no subscribe method, and its sessions close after each call, so there is no session a `notifications/resources/updated` could reach.
notes_by_num.12: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: the adapter has no subscribe API. `MCPTool.session` is the raw SDK `ClientSession`, and `subscribe_resource` / `unsubscribe_resource` there deliver the update.
notes_by_num.13: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1 has no subscribe API. `MCPServerStdio.session` is the raw SDK `ClientSession`, and `subscribe_resource` / `unsubscribe_resource` on it worked, with the update reaching the server's `message_handler`. That route belongs to the SDK, not the adapter.
notes_by_num.14: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: `MCPToolset` has no subscribe API. That route belongs to the SDK, not the adapter.
notes_by_num.15: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: the plugin has no subscribe API; subscribing works only on the raw `ClientSession` it exposes as `plugin.session`.
notes_by_num.16: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` exposes only `get_tools()`; there is no subscribe route and no hook for `notifications/resources/updated`.
notes_by_num.17: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPClient` has no subscribe method, and its `ClientSession` is private (`_background_thread_session`), so a caller cannot subscribe to a resource.
notes_by_num.18: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `subscribeResource` / `unsubscribeResource` and the update notification work, but @genkit-ai/mcp has no API for it and registers no notification handler; it works only on the SDK `Client` that the public getter `GenkitMcpClient.mcpClient` hands out (route `session`).
notes_by_num.19: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): there is no API that sends `resources/subscribe` or `resources/unsubscribe`.
notes_by_num.20: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: reachable only on a raw `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `Client` from `MCPSessionManager.createSession()`, a public export of `@google/adk/tools/mcp`: `subscribeResource` / `unsubscribeResource` with a `ResourceUpdatedNotificationSchema` handler delivered the update, and none after unsubscribing. `MCPToolset` has no subscribe method, and its per-call sessions close before an update could arrive.
notes_by_num.21: Mastra 2.2.0: `resources.subscribe('src', uri)` rejects with `subscriptions/listen needs MCP 2026-07-28` against a 2025-11-25 server. notes_by_num.22: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the `MCPServer` interface has `listResources`, `listResourceTemplates` and `readResource`, but no `resources/subscribe` method and no hook for `notifications/resources/updated`.
notes_by_num.23: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient` has no subscribe method. The generic `request('resources/subscribe')` and `request('resources/unsubscribe')`, with `onNotification('notifications/resources/updated')`, subscribe, deliver the update and unsubscribe, but only with the caller naming each wire method.
notes_by_num.24: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): MCPClient has no `resources/subscribe` or `unsubscribe` method and no handler for `notifications/resources/updated`. 2.0.73 adds `experimental_events`, a webhook API for `events/subscribe` and `events/unsubscribe`, which is a separate surface and does not cover resource updates.
notes_by_num.25: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): the `resourceSubscriptions` server option subscribes at connect and `onResourcesUpdated` receives the update, but the adapter has no unsubscribe method and the list is fixed for the connection.
notes_by_num.26: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `McpTool.getMcpSession().subscribeResource` and `unsubscribeResource` reach the server, but `McpSessionManager` builds the client with no `resourcesUpdateConsumer` and ADK offers no way to add one, so no `notifications/resources/updated` reaches the caller.
notes_by_num.27: Koog 1.3.0-beta: no Koog API. `Client.subscribeResource` / `unsubscribeResource` and a `notifications/resources/updated` handler set with `Client.setNotificationHandler` on the underlying Kotlin SDK `Client` deliver the update.
notes_by_num.28: Spring AI 2.0.1: the starter has no subscription API. `McpSyncClient.subscribeResource` and `unsubscribeResource` on the published client bean work, and updates arrive only through a `resourcesUpdateConsumer` set in an `McpClientCustomizer<McpClient.SyncSpec>` bean; no update came after unsubscribing.
notes_by_num.29: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `Subscribe` on.

resources-list.title: `resources/list`
resources-list.description: Lists the resources a server exposes, each identified by a URI and described with a name, title, MIME type and optional size.
resources-list.question: Can the agent discover the server's resources at all?
resources-list.notes: 18 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 3 changed or retained elsewhere, 10 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so `resources/list` is unreachable.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `beeai_framework.tools.mcp` has `MCPTool` only. `MCPTool.from_client` lists and wraps tools, and BeeAI has no MCP resource or prompt API.
notes_by_num.3: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` exposes only `tools`. It has no resource or prompt API, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.

notes_by_num.5: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy's MCP support is `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`, which converts one tool. It has no resource or prompt API, so resources and prompts stay on the caller's MCP session.

resources-list-changed.title: `notifications/resources/list_changed`
resources-list-changed.description: The notification a server sends when the set of available resources changes.
resources-list-changed.question: Does the framework notice when the resource list changes?
resources-list-changed.notes: 10 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 8 changed or retained elsewhere, 13 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so a resources list_changed notification has nothing to refresh, and no hook hears it.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no resource listing to refresh; BeeAI converts tools only and has no notification hook.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: The workbench registers no message handler, so no hook hears the notification; its `list_resources` asks the server every time, so the next listing shows the change.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` exposes only `tools`. It has no resource or prompt API, so there is no list for a notification to refresh.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient` has `list_tools`, `call_tool`, `list_prompts` and `get_prompt` and no resource API, and `Agent(mcps=...)` turns only the tools into `BaseTool`s, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy's MCP support is `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`, which converts one tool. It has no resource or prompt API, so resources and prompts stay on the caller's MCP session. No listing means no change to see.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` takes no message handler, so nothing an application registers hears the notification. `list_resources` asks the server on every call, so the next list showed the added resource anyway.
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` with no message handler, and `MCPToolset` has no resource API, so `notifications/resources/list_changed` reaches nothing.
notes_by_num.9: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` takes no message handler and closes its session after every call (over stdio it also starts a fresh server process per call), so no session is open to hear `notifications/resources/list_changed`, and the next listing did not show the added resource.
notes_by_num.10: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: there is no resource API to relist, so a resources list_changed notification reaches `message_handler` and changes nothing the agent can see.
notes_by_num.11: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `MCPPluginBase` has no resource list to refresh.
notes_by_num.12: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` exposes only `get_tools()`. It has no resource or prompt API, so there is no list for a notification to refresh.
notes_by_num.13: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `on_tools_changed` is the only change hook, and it covers tools only. Nothing hears the resources notification, but `list_resources_sync` asks the server every time, so the next listing shows the change.
notes_by_num.14: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: no handler for `notifications/resources/list_changed` is registered and there is no change hook. Re-listing did not show the change either: `getActiveResources` also calls `resources/templates/list`, the notify fixture does not implement it, and the `-32601` error discards the whole resource list, so both lists came back empty.
notes_by_num.15: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPToolset` opens a new session for every operation (`getTools`, `listResources`, `readResource`, each tool call) and closes it after; over stdio that is a new server process each time. No session outlives the call that changed the list, and over stdio the added resource dies with its process, so the next `listResources` matched the one before.
notes_by_num.16: Mastra 2.2.0 against a 2025-11-25 server: `onListChanged('src', fn)` installs the handler, and it fired and the next list showed the change. But the call itself rejects with `subscriptions/listen needs MCP 2026-07-28`, because it also tries to open a 2026-07-28 stream. Code that awaits the registration sees an error for a hook that works.
notes_by_num.17: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: no handler hears `notifications/resources/list_changed`; the change shows only because the next `listResources` asks the server again.
notes_by_num.18: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): MCPClient registers no notification handler: a server notification reaches only `onUncaughtError`, as an "Unsupported message type" error that does not name the notification. `listResources()` fetches on every call, so the next list shows the added resource.
notes_by_num.19: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: The adapter registers no `resourcesChangeConsumer` consumer, so nothing tells the agent the list changed. The next `McpToolset.getTools` call (or session `listResources`) lists again and shows the change.
notes_by_num.20: Koog 1.3.0-beta: Koog exposes only tools and registers no list-changed handler. The next `Client.listResources` on the underlying Kotlin SDK `Client` shows the change.
notes_by_num.21: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): a `ResourceListChangedHandler` on the caller's `*mcp.Client` hears the notification, but mcptoolset lists only tools, so the agent has no resources list to refresh.

resources-read.title: `resources/read`
resources-read.description: Reads the contents behind a resource URI, which may return several contents for one request.
resources-read.question: Can the agent read a resource's contents through the framework?
resources-read.notes: 19 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 2 changed or retained elsewhere, 10 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so `resources/read` is unreachable.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `beeai_framework.tools.mcp` has `MCPTool` only. `MCPTool.from_client` lists and wraps tools, and BeeAI has no MCP resource or prompt API.
notes_by_num.3: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` exposes only `tools`. It has no resource or prompt API, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient` has `list_tools`, `call_tool`, `list_prompts` and `get_prompt` and no resource API, and `Agent(mcps=...)` turns only the tools into `BaseTool`s, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes_by_num.5: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy's MCP support is `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`, which converts one tool. It has no resource or prompt API, so resources and prompts stay on the caller's MCP session.
notes_by_num.6: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` wraps tools as Haystack `Tool`s and has no resource or prompt API, and the `ClientSession` it opens is private to `MCPToolset._worker._client`, so there is no route to `resources/read`.
notes_by_num.7: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: `MCPTool` has no resource or resource-template API; `resources/list`, `resources/read` and `resources/templates/list` are never sent. (`MCPSkillsSource` reads resources, but only `skill://index.json` and the skills it names.)
notes_by_num.8: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: a text resource is returned as a bare string. The contents arrive intact, but the `uri` and `mimeType` that identify them are dropped, so the agent cannot tell which resource it just read.
notes_by_num.9: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `MCPPluginBase` loads tools and prompts only; it has no resource API.
notes_by_num.10: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` exposes only `get_tools()`, and the `ClientSession` lives on the private `MCPClient._adapter`. It has no resource or prompt API, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes_by_num.11: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: a resource action returns `{ content: [{ text } | { media: { contentType, url } }] }`: the text survives, but the read result keeps neither the `uri` nor the text's `mimeType` (a blob keeps its type as the media `contentType`).
notes_by_num.12: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `ReadResource` on.

prompts-list.title: `prompts/list`
prompts-list.description: Lists the prompt templates a server exposes, with their names, titles, descriptions and argument definitions.
prompts-list.question: Can the agent discover the server's prompts?
prompts-list.notes: 12 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 5 changed or retained elsewhere, 14 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so `prompts/list` is unreachable.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `beeai_framework.tools.mcp` has `MCPTool` only. `MCPTool.from_client` lists and wraps tools, and BeeAI has no MCP resource or prompt API.
notes_by_num.3: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` exposes only `tools`. It has no resource or prompt API, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient.list_prompts` returns each prompt as `name`, `description` and `arguments` only, so the prompt's `title` is dropped. The agent itself is not handed prompts; they are reachable only by calling `MCPClient` directly.
notes_by_num.5: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy's MCP support is `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`, which converts one tool. It has no resource or prompt API, so resources and prompts stay on the caller's MCP session.
notes_by_num.6: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` has no prompt methods; `prompts/list` is never sent.
notes_by_num.7: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` wraps tools as Haystack `Tool`s and has no resource or prompt API, and the `ClientSession` it opens is private to `MCPToolset._worker._client`, so there is no route to `prompts/list`.
notes_by_num.8: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: the package has no API for listing prompts. `load_mcp_prompt` can expand a prompt the caller already knows by name, but nothing tells the agent which prompts exist or what arguments they take.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: the package has no API for listing prompts. `load_mcp_prompt` can expand a prompt the caller already knows by name, but nothing tells the agent which prompts exist or what arguments they take.
notes_by_num.10: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: prompts are listed only as the `FunctionTool`s `load_prompts` builds, one per prompt, which the model can call like tools. Name, description and arguments survive; the prompt's `title` does not.
notes_by_num.11: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: prompts become KernelFunctions (`load_prompts`); a prompt's name, description and arguments survive, its title does not.
notes_by_num.12: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` exposes only `get_tools()`, and the `ClientSession` lives on the private `MCPClient._adapter`. It has no resource or prompt API, so an agent built on it cannot reach this at all.
notes_by_num.13: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `getActivePrompts` returns an `ExecutablePrompt` per MCP prompt whose `ref.metadata` keeps `description` and `arguments`; `title` is not kept.
notes_by_num.14: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPToolset` has no prompt API (`listPrompts`), and ADK adds none elsewhere.
notes_by_num.15: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the `MCPServer` interface (agents-core `src/mcp.ts`) has tools and resources methods but no prompts method.
notes_by_num.16: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient` has no prompts method; `prompts/list` is reachable only by hand through the generic `request()`.
notes_by_num.17: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `MCPAdapter` has no prompts API (no list, get or loader for prompts), so there is no route to `prompts/list`.
notes_by_num.18: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpPrompt` holds `name`, `description` and `arguments`; `prompts/list` loses each prompt's `title`.
notes_by_num.19: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `ListPrompts` on.

prompts-list-changed.title: `notifications/prompts/list_changed`
prompts-list-changed.description: The notification a server sends when the set of available prompts changes.
prompts-list-changed.question: Does the framework notice when the prompt list changes?
prompts-list-changed.notes: 7 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 8 changed or retained elsewhere, 16 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` lists and calls tools only; it has no resource or prompt API, so a prompts list_changed notification has nothing to refresh, and no hook hears it.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no prompt listing to refresh; BeeAI converts tools only and has no notification hook.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: The workbench registers no message handler, so no hook hears the notification; its `list_prompts` asks the server every time, so the next listing shows the change.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` exposes only `tools`. It has no resource or prompt API, so there is no list for a notification to refresh.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` with no message handler and has no list-changed hook, so `notifications/prompts/list_changed` goes unseen and the next list is whatever the caller asks for again.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy's MCP support is `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool`, which converts one tool. It has no resource or prompt API, so resources and prompts stay on the caller's MCP session. No listing means no change to see.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` has no prompt methods, so there is no list for a notification to refresh.
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` with no message handler, and `MCPToolset` has no prompt API, so `notifications/prompts/list_changed` reaches nothing.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: there is no prompt listing API (`load_mcp_prompt` expands one prompt by name), so an added prompt cannot be discovered through the adapter whatever the notification says.
notes_by_num.10: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: there is no prompt listing API (`load_mcp_prompt` expands one prompt by name), so an added prompt cannot be discovered through the adapter whatever the notification says.
notes_by_num.11: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` takes no message handler and closes its session after every call (over stdio it also starts a fresh server process per call), so no session is open to hear `notifications/prompts/list_changed`, and the next `list_prompts` did not show the added prompt.
notes_by_num.12: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: the default `message_handler` awaits `load_prompts()` inside the MCP session's receive loop, deadlocking the session until the request times out; the prompt list stays stale.
notes_by_num.13: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` exposes only `get_tools()`. It has no resource or prompt API, so there is no list for a notification to refresh.
notes_by_num.14: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `on_tools_changed` is the only change hook, and it covers tools only. Nothing hears the prompts notification, but `list_prompts_sync` asks the server every time, so the next listing shows the change.
notes_by_num.15: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: no handler for `notifications/prompts/list_changed` is registered and there is no change hook; each `getActivePrompts` call lists again, so a caller that re-lists sees the added prompt.
notes_by_num.16: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPToolset` has no prompt listing API, so there is nothing to refresh.
notes_by_num.17: Mastra 2.2.0 against a 2025-11-25 server: `onListChanged('src', fn)` installs the handler, and it fired and the next list showed the change. But the call itself rejects with `subscriptions/listen needs MCP 2026-07-28`, because it also tries to open a 2026-07-28 stream. Code that awaits the registration sees an error for a hook that works.
notes_by_num.18: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: no prompts method and no notification hook, so a prompt-list change has no route to the caller.
notes_by_num.19: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `onNotification` would hear `notifications/prompts/list_changed`, but `McpClient` has no prompts method to list the change with.
notes_by_num.20: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): MCPClient registers no notification handler: a server notification reaches only `onUncaughtError`, as an "Unsupported message type" error that does not name the notification. `experimental_listPrompts()` fetches on every call, so the next list shows the added prompt.
notes_by_num.21: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): there is an `onPromptsListChanged` server option, but with no prompts API there is nothing to relist, so the notification has no route to the application.
notes_by_num.22: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: The adapter registers no `promptsChangeConsumer` consumer, so nothing tells the agent the list changed. The next `McpToolset.getTools` call (or session `listPrompts`) lists again and shows the change.
notes_by_num.23: Koog 1.3.0-beta: same as resources: no hook, and the next `Client.listPrompts` on the underlying `Client` shows the change.
notes_by_num.24: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): a `PromptListChangedHandler` on the caller's `*mcp.Client` hears the notification, but mcptoolset lists only tools, so the agent has no prompts list to refresh.

elicitation-form-mode.title: `elicitation/create` (form)
elicitation-form-mode.description: A server request for structured user input, described by a restricted flat JSON Schema and answered with accept, decline or cancel.
elicitation-form-mode.question: Can a server ask the user a question through this framework?
elicitation-form-mode.notes: 11 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 4 changed or retained elsewhere, 16 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` builds its fastmcp `Client` with no elicitation handler and exposes no hook to add one, so form elicitation is refused.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no elicitation handler. Form elicitation works only on a `ClientSession` the caller builds and hands `MCPTool.from_client`, which BeeAI uses as given; the session BeeAI opens itself for a transport has no callbacks.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench` opens its `ClientSession` with no elicitation callback and takes none, so the server's request is refused.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` takes only server parameters, and mcpadapt opens its `ClientSession` with no callbacks, so the client declares no elicitation capability and the server's `elicitation/create` is refused (`Elicitation not supported`).
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient.connect` builds its `ClientSession` from the transport streams alone, with no `elicitation_callback`, and `MCPServerStdio`/`MCPServerHTTP`/`MCPServerSSE` take no hook for it, so the client does not declare the capability and the server's request is refused.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy takes no elicitation handler. The server's request is answered only by a `elicitation_callback` registered on the caller's own `mcp.Client`, which DSPy is handed by `Tool.from_mcp_tool` and never configures. DSPy itself offers no route.
notes_by_num.7: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession(read, write)` with no sampling, elicitation, roots or message callback, and neither the server info nor `MCPToolset` takes one, so the server's form-mode `elicitation/create` got no answer and the tool call failed.
notes_by_num.8: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` takes a `sampling_callback` and nothing for elicitation, so the client declares no elicitation capability and the server's `elicitation/create` is refused (`Elicitation not supported`).
notes_by_num.9: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: The `ClientSession` that `MCPTool.connect` builds gets only `message_handler`, `logging_callback` and `sampling_callback`, and `MCPTool` has no parameter for this, so the SDK answers the server with an error.
notes_by_num.10: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: `MCPServerStdio` forwards only `message_handler` to its `ClientSession`, which sees notifications, not requests. With no elicitation hook the client declares no elicitation capability and the server's `elicitation/create` is refused (`Elicitation not supported`).
notes_by_num.11: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `MCPPluginBase` opens its ClientSession with no `elicitation_callback` and takes none.
notes_by_num.12: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` takes server parameters, `adapter_kwargs` and `structured_output` only, and mcpadapt opens its `ClientSession` with no callbacks, so the client declares no elicitation capability and the server's `elicitation/create` is refused (`Elicitation not supported`).
notes_by_num.13: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `GenkitMcpClient` builds its SDK `Client` with only the `roots` capability and handler, so `elicitation/create` gets `Method not found` and there is no option to add a handler.
notes_by_num.14: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPSessionManager.createSession` builds `new Client({name: 'MCPClient', version: '1.0.0'})` with no capabilities and no request handlers, and `MCPToolset` takes no client hooks. `elicitation/create` is refused (`Method not found`).
notes_by_num.15: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the `MCPServerStdio` / `MCPServerStreamableHttp` options take no sampling, elicitation or roots handler, and the SDK registers none on the MCP client it builds, so the server's form-mode `elicitation/create` request is answered with Method not found.
notes_by_num.16: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient` takes no elicitation handler and registers none, so an `elicitation/create` request is answered with Method not found. A caller could hand-register one with `setRequestHandler` and declare the capability through the `capabilities` option, which is protocol work rather than a client feature.

elicitation-url-mode.title: `elicitation/create` (URL)
elicitation-url-mode.description: A server request that sends the user out of band to a URL, for interactions such as sign-in that must not pass through the client.
elicitation-url-mode.question: Can the framework hand a user off to an external URL and resume?
elicitation-url-mode.notes: 9 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 5 changed or retained elsewhere, 17 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` builds its fastmcp `Client` with no elicitation handler and exposes no hook to add one, so URL elicitation is refused.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no elicitation handler. URL elicitation works only on a `ClientSession` the caller builds and hands `MCPTool.from_client`, which BeeAI uses as given; the session BeeAI opens itself for a transport has no callbacks.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench` opens its `ClientSession` with no elicitation callback and takes none, so the server's request is refused.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` takes only server parameters, and mcpadapt opens its `ClientSession` with no callbacks, so the client declares no elicitation capability and the server's `elicitation/create` is refused (`Elicitation not supported`).
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient.connect` builds its `ClientSession` from the transport streams alone, with no `elicitation_callback`, and `MCPServerStdio`/`MCPServerHTTP`/`MCPServerSSE` take no hook for it, so the client does not declare the capability and the server's request is refused.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy takes no elicitation handler. The server's request is answered only by a `elicitation_callback` registered on the caller's own `mcp.Client`, which DSPy is handed by `Tool.from_mcp_tool` and never configures. DSPy itself offers no route.
notes_by_num.7: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession(read, write)` with no sampling, elicitation, roots or message callback, and neither the server info nor `MCPToolset` takes one, so the server's URL-mode `elicitation/create` got no answer and the tool call failed.
notes_by_num.8: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` takes a `sampling_callback` and nothing for elicitation, so the client declares no elicitation capability and the server's URL-mode `elicitation/create` is refused (`Elicitation not supported`).
notes_by_num.9: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: The `ClientSession` that `MCPTool.connect` builds gets only `message_handler`, `logging_callback` and `sampling_callback`, and `MCPTool` has no parameter for this, so the SDK answers the server with an error.
notes_by_num.10: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: `MCPServerStdio` forwards only `message_handler` to its `ClientSession`, which sees notifications, not requests. With no elicitation hook the client declares no elicitation capability and the server's `elicitation/create` is refused (`Elicitation not supported`).
notes_by_num.11: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `MCPPluginBase` opens its ClientSession with no `elicitation_callback` and takes none.
notes_by_num.12: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` takes server parameters, `adapter_kwargs` and `structured_output` only, and mcpadapt opens its `ClientSession` with no callbacks, so the client declares no elicitation capability and the server's URL-mode `elicitation/create` is refused (`Elicitation not supported`).
notes_by_num.13: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `GenkitMcpClient` builds its SDK `Client` with only the `roots` capability and handler, so a URL-mode `elicitation/create` gets `Method not found` and there is no option to add a handler.

notes_by_num.19: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `McpSessionManager` builds the `McpSyncClient` with empty client capabilities and no elicitation handler, and neither `McpToolset` nor `McpTool` takes one, so `elicitation/create` is answered `Method not found`.
notes_by_num.20: Koog 1.3.0-beta: no Koog API. `Client.setElicitationHandler` on the Kotlin SDK `Client` before `fromClient` answers URL-mode `elicitation/create`.

roots-list-changed.question: Does this framework emit the notification when its roots change?

roots-list-changed.summary: The cell asks whether the adapter announces a roots change through its own API.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` exposes no roots and no way to change them, so the client never sends `notifications/roots/list_changed`.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no roots API. notifications/roots/list_changed is sent only on a `ClientSession` the caller builds and hands `MCPTool.from_client`, which BeeAI uses as given; the session BeeAI opens itself for a transport has no callbacks.

sampling-create-message.title: `sampling/createMessage`
sampling-create-message.description: A server request asking the client's model for a generation, so the server can use an LLM without holding model credentials of its own.
sampling-create-message.question: Can a server borrow the client's model through this framework?
sampling-create-message.notes: 8 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 7 changed or retained elsewhere, 16 dropped. The cell asks whether the adapter answers it through its own API.
sampling-create-message.summary: The cell asks whether the adapter answers it through its own API.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` builds its fastmcp `Client` with no sampling handler and exposes no hook to add one, so a server's `sampling/createMessage` is refused.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no sampling handler. Sampling works only on a `ClientSession` the caller builds and hands `MCPTool.from_client`, which BeeAI uses as given; the session BeeAI opens itself for a transport has no callbacks.
notes_by_num.3: CrewAI 1.15.26: `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` takes only server parameters, and mcpadapt opens its `ClientSession` with no callbacks, so the client declares no sampling capability and the server's `sampling/createMessage` is refused (`Sampling not supported`).
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient.connect` builds its `ClientSession` from the transport streams alone, with no `sampling_callback`, and `MCPServerStdio`/`MCPServerHTTP`/`MCPServerSSE` take no hook for it, so the client does not declare the capability and the server's request is refused.
notes_by_num.5: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy takes no sampling handler. The server's request is answered only by a `sampling_callback` registered on the caller's own `mcp.Client`, which DSPy is handed by `Tool.from_mcp_tool` and never configures. DSPy itself offers no route.
notes_by_num.6: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession(read, write)` with no sampling, elicitation, roots or message callback, and neither the server info nor `MCPToolset` takes one, so the server's `sampling/createMessage` got no answer and the tool call failed.
notes_by_num.7: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: the adapter has no sampling API. A `sampling_callback` put in the connection's `session_kwargs` is forwarded unread to the MCP SDK's `ClientSession` and answers the request, so it works, but only by writing against the SDK rather than the adapter.
notes_by_num.8: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: the adapter has no sampling API. A `sampling_callback` put in the connection's `session_kwargs` is forwarded unread to the MCP SDK's `ClientSession` and answers the request, so it works, but only by writing against the SDK rather than the adapter.
notes_by_num.9: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: `MCPServerStdio` forwards only `message_handler` to its `ClientSession`, which sees notifications, not requests. With no sampling hook the client declares no sampling capability and the server's `sampling/createMessage` is refused (`Sampling not supported`).
notes_by_num.10: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `smolagents.MCPClient` takes server parameters, `adapter_kwargs` and `structured_output` only, and mcpadapt opens its `ClientSession` with no callbacks, so the client declares no sampling capability and the server's `sampling/createMessage` is refused (`Sampling not supported`).
notes_by_num.11: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPClient` passes its `ClientSession` an `elicitation_callback` only. There is no sampling parameter, so the server's `sampling/createMessage` is refused.
notes_by_num.12: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `GenkitMcpClient` builds its SDK `Client` with only `{ roots: { listChanged: true } }` and registers only a `roots/list` handler, so `sampling/createMessage` gets `Method not found` and there is no option to add a handler.
notes_by_num.13: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the client declares the sampling capability, but the runtime answers every `sampling/createMessage` itself with `stopReason: "cancelled"` and the text "The user cancelled the request.". notes_by_num.14: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPSessionManager.createSession` builds `new Client({name: 'MCPClient', version: '1.0.0'})` with no capabilities and no request handlers, and `MCPToolset` takes no client hooks. `sampling/createMessage` is refused (`Method not found`).
notes_by_num.15: Mastra 2.2.0: `@mastra/mcp` documents the deprecated sampling capability as unsupported and registers no handler, so the server's `sampling/createMessage` gets `Method not found`.
notes_by_num.16: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the `MCPServerStdio` / `MCPServerStreamableHttp` options take no sampling, elicitation or roots handler, and the SDK registers none on the MCP client it builds, so the server's `sampling/createMessage` request is answered with Method not found.
notes_by_num.17: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient` takes no sampling handler and registers none, so a `sampling/createMessage` request is answered with Method not found.

notes_by_num.21: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `McpSessionManager` builds the `McpSyncClient` with empty client capabilities and no sampling handler, and neither `McpToolset` nor `McpTool` takes one, so the server's `sampling/createMessage` is answered `Method not found`.
