sampling-tools.title: Sampling `tools` / `toolChoice`
sampling-tools.description: Request-scoped tool use inside a sampling call, driving a multi-turn tool loop with `tool_use` and `tool_result` content and a `toolUse` stop reason.
sampling-tools.question: Does the framework run the sampling tool loop, or only single-shot generation?
sampling-tools.notes: 3 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 6 changed or retained elsewhere, 22 dropped. The cell asks whether the adapter runs the sampling tool loop through its own API.
sampling-tools.summary: The cell asks whether the adapter runs the sampling tool loop through its own API.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` builds its fastmcp `Client` with no sampling handler, so sampling with tools is refused like any other sampling request.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no sampling handler. Sampling with tools works only on a `ClientSession` the caller builds and hands `MCPTool.from_client`, which BeeAI uses as given; the session BeeAI opens itself for a transport has no callbacks.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench(model_client=...)` answers sampling, but its session declares plain `sampling` without `tools` and `McpSessionActor` never forwards a request's tools to the model client, so a tool-enabled sampling request is refused.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26: no sampling hook, so the client cannot declare `sampling.tools` and the server's SDK refuses to send a tools-bearing request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`).
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient.connect` builds its `ClientSession` from the transport streams alone, with no `sampling_callback`, and `MCPServerStdio`/`MCPServerHTTP`/`MCPServerSSE` take no hook for it, so the client does not declare the capability and the server's request is refused.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy takes no sampling handler. The server's request is answered only by a `sampling_callback` with `sampling_capabilities` registered on the caller's own `mcp.Client`, which DSPy is handed by `Tool.from_mcp_tool` and never configures. DSPy itself offers no route.
notes_by_num.7: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession(read, write)` with no sampling, elicitation, roots or message callback, and neither the server info nor `MCPToolset` takes one, so the server's `sampling/createMessage` with tools got no answer and the tool call failed.
notes_by_num.8: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: through `session_kwargs` (a `sampling_callback` plus `sampling_capabilities` with `tools`), forwarded unread to the MCP SDK, the two-turn tool loop completed: `tool_use`, the server's `tool_result`, then a final answer. The adapter itself offers neither.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: through `session_kwargs` (a `sampling_callback` plus `sampling_capabilities` with `tools`), forwarded unread to the MCP SDK, the two-turn tool loop completed: `tool_use`, the server's `tool_result`, then a final answer. The adapter itself offers neither.
notes_by_num.10: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient(sampling_callback=...)` forwards the callback but not `sampling_capabilities`, so the client never declares `sampling.tools` and the server's tools-enabled `sampling/createMessage` is refused.
notes_by_num.11: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: no sampling hook, so the client cannot declare `sampling.tools` and the server's SDK refuses to send a tools-bearing request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`).
notes_by_num.12: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: `MCPToolset(sampling_handler=...)` declares plain `sampling` without `tools`, so a tools-bearing request is refused. Declaring `sampling.tools` takes `toolset.client.set_sampling_callback(..., sampling_capabilities=...)` on the wrapped fastmcp `Client`; through that the two-turn tool loop completed.
notes_by_num.13: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: the plugin's `sampling_callback` forwards only messages, system prompt, temperature and max tokens to the kernel's chat service, and the session declares no `sampling.tools` capability, so the server refuses a tool-enabled request.
notes_by_num.14: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): no sampling hook, so the client cannot declare `sampling.tools` and the server's SDK refuses to send a tools-bearing request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`).
notes_by_num.15: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPClient` has no sampling parameter, so it cannot declare `sampling.tools` or answer a tool-enabled sampling request.
notes_by_num.16: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: no sampling capability is declared (only `roots`), so a sampling request with tools is refused and there is no option to add a handler.
notes_by_num.17: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the runtime does not declare sampling tool support, so the server's tool-bearing sampling request failed with "Client does not support sampling tools capability".
notes_by_num.18: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPSessionManager.createSession` builds `new Client({name: 'MCPClient', version: '1.0.0'})` with no capabilities and no request handlers, and `MCPToolset` takes no client hooks. The tools-enabled `sampling/createMessage` is refused.
notes_by_num.19: Mastra 2.2.0: no sampling handler and no way to declare `sampling.tools`, so the server's SDK refuses to send the request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`).
notes_by_num.20: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the client declares no sampling capability, so the server's sampling-with-tools request is refused before any handler could run; the SDK has no sampling hook.
notes_by_num.21: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient` takes no sampling handler and declares no sampling capability, so the server refuses to send a tool-enabled sampling request.
notes_by_num.22: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): no sampling support, so the server refuses the tool-enabled request ("Client does not support sampling tools capability").
notes_by_num.23: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): there is no sampling handler of any kind, so sampling with tools has no route either.
notes_by_num.24: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `DefaultMcpClient` declares no `sampling` capability, so the server refuses tool-enabled sampling with `Client does not support sampling tools capability`.
notes_by_num.25: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `McpSessionManager` builds the `McpSyncClient` with empty client capabilities and no sampling handler, and neither `McpToolset` nor `McpTool` takes one, so the server refuses the request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`).
notes_by_num.26: Koog 1.3.0-beta: not reachable. The server's SDK refuses the request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`): Kotlin SDK 0.11.1's client capabilities have no sampling `tools` flag, and its `CreateMessageResult` cannot carry a `tool_use` block.
notes_by_num.27: Spring AI 2.0.1: `McpSchema.CreateMessageRequest` in MCP Java SDK 2.0.0 has no tools field, so `@McpSampling` cannot declare `sampling.tools` and the server's SDK refuses the tools-bearing request (`Client does not support sampling tools capability`).
notes_by_num.28: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): mcptoolset has no sampling option. A `mcp.ClientOptions.CreateMessageWithToolsHandler` set on the `*mcp.Client` the caller passes as `mcptoolset.Config.Client` answers the server's request, so it works, but only by configuring go-sdk rather than the toolset.

completion-complete.title: `completion/complete`
completion-complete.description: Returns autocomplete suggestions for a prompt argument or a resource template variable, capped at 100 values per response.
completion-complete.question: Can the framework ask the server to complete an argument value?
completion-complete.notes: 2 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 18 changed or retained elsewhere, 11 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` has no completion method; `completion/complete` works only through `MCPTools.session`, the fastmcp `Client` it exposes (`Client.complete`).
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no completion API. `completion/complete` works only on a `ClientSession` the caller builds and hands `MCPTool.from_client`, which BeeAI uses as given; the session BeeAI opens itself for a transport has no callbacks, via `ClientSession.complete`.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench` has no completion method, and its `ClientSession` is private to `McpSessionActor`.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26: `MCPServerAdapter` has no completion API, and its sessions are private.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient` has no completion API. `completion/complete` works only through the public `MCPClient.session` (`session.complete(...)`), a raw MCP `ClientSession`, which the probe used.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy has no completion API. `completion/complete` works only through `complete` on the caller's own `mcp.Client`, which DSPy is handed by `Tool.from_mcp_tool` and never configures. DSPy itself offers no route.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` has no completion API. `MCPSessionManager.create_session()`, the session manager `McpToolset` and `McpTool` are built on, hands out the raw mcp `ClientSession`, and `complete(...)` on it works.
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` wraps tools as Haystack `Tool`s and has no resource or prompt API, and the `ClientSession` it opens is private to `MCPToolset._worker._client`, so there is no route to `completion/complete`.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: the adapter has no completion API. `MultiServerMCPClient.session().complete(...)` works on the raw mcp `ClientSession` it hands out.
notes_by_num.10: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: the adapter has no completion API. `MultiServerMCPClient.session().complete(...)` works on the raw mcp `ClientSession` it hands out.
notes_by_num.11: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` has no completion method, and the `ClientSession` it opens exists only inside the private `_run_session`, so no caller can send `completion/complete`.
notes_by_num.12: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: the adapter has no completion API. `MCPTool.session.complete(...)` works on the raw mcp `ClientSession` the tool exposes.
notes_by_num.13: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: the adapter has no completion API. `MCPServer.session.complete(...)` works on the raw mcp `ClientSession`.
notes_by_num.14: Pydantic AI 2.54.0: `MCPToolset` has no completion API. `toolset.client.complete(...)` works on the FastMCP client the toolset exposes.
notes_by_num.15: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: the plugin has no completion API; it works only on the raw `ClientSession` exposed as `plugin.session`.
notes_by_num.16: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `MCPClient` has no completion API, and the session lives on the private `MCPClient._adapter`.
notes_by_num.17: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPClient` has no completion method, and the `ClientSession` it would need runs privately on the client's background thread (`_background_thread_session`), so a caller has no route to `completion/complete`.
notes_by_num.18: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `complete` answers for both the prompt argument and the resource template, but @genkit-ai/mcp has no API for it and registers no notification handler; it works only on the SDK `Client` that the public getter `GenkitMcpClient.mcpClient` hands out (route `session`).
notes_by_num.19: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): there is no completion API. Nothing in `CopilotSession` or `session.rpc.mcp` sends `completion/complete` to an MCP server.
notes_by_num.20: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: reachable only on a raw `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `Client` from `MCPSessionManager.createSession()`, a public export of `@google/adk/tools/mcp` (`complete`). `MCPToolset` has no completion API.
notes_by_num.21: Mastra 2.2.0: `MCPClient` does not wrap completion. The SDK client's `complete` sits behind the private `mcpClientsById` field.
notes_by_num.22: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `MCPServer` has no completion method. The MCP client's `complete` sits in the protected `session` field, so it is not a route a user is given.
notes_by_num.23: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient` has no completion method. The public generic `request('completion/complete', ...)` gets the server's values back, but the caller names the wire method and reads the raw result.
notes_by_num.24: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): `MCPAdapter` has no completion method. `completion/complete` is reachable only on the `@modelcontextprotocol/client` `Client` that `getClient(server)` hands out.
notes_by_num.25: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpClient` has no `completion/complete` method, so `DefaultMcpClient` never sends one.
notes_by_num.26: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: No ADK API. `McpTool.getMcpSession().completeCompletion` on the underlying `McpSyncClient` completes both the prompt argument and the resource template argument.
notes_by_num.27: Koog 1.3.0-beta: no Koog API. `Client.complete` on the underlying Kotlin SDK `Client` completes both the prompt argument and the resource template argument.
notes_by_num.28: Spring AI 2.0.1: the starter has no completion API. `McpSyncClient.completeCompletion` on the client bean the starter publishes answers both the prompt and the resource-template argument, so this goes through the session rather than the adapter.
notes_by_num.29: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `Complete` on.

logging-notifications.title: `notifications/message`
logging-notifications.description: Structured server log records at RFC 5424 levels, enabled per request through a log level in that request's `_meta`.
logging-notifications.question: Can a developer see the server's own logs through the framework?
logging-notifications.notes: 11 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 6 changed or retained elsewhere, 14 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` takes no log handler; its fastmcp `Client` uses fastmcp's default, which writes server log messages to Python logging, so none reaches the agent or caller.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no logging hook. Log messages reach the caller only on a `ClientSession` the caller builds and hands `MCPTool.from_client`, which BeeAI uses as given; the session BeeAI opens itself for a transport has no callbacks, via `logging_callback`.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench` opens its `ClientSession` without a `logging_callback`; the server's `notifications/message` reach no caller.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26: mcpadapt builds its `ClientSession` without a `logging_callback`. The server's `notifications/message` arrive, and the SDK's default handler drops them before any caller sees them.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient.connect` builds its `ClientSession` from the transport streams alone, with no `logging_callback`, and `MCPServerStdio`/`MCPServerHTTP`/`MCPServerSSE` take no hook for it, so the server's `notifications/message` reach nothing.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy takes no log handler. Server log messages reach a caller only through a `logging_callback` on the caller's own `mcp.Client`, which DSPy is handed by `Tool.from_mcp_tool` and never configures. DSPy itself offers no route.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` has no logging hook, and the `ClientSession` its `MCPSessionManager` builds is given no `logging_callback`. The server's `notifications/message` arrive, and the SDK's default handler drops them before any caller sees them.
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` without a `logging_callback` and `MCPToolset` takes no log handler, so the server's five `notifications/message` reached the caller as nothing.
notes_by_num.9: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` builds its `ClientSession` without a `logging_callback`. The server's `notifications/message` arrive and the SDK's default handler drops them. `tool_call_logs_callback` collects Python `logging` records from the client process, not MCP log notifications.
notes_by_num.10: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt builds its `ClientSession` without a `logging_callback`. The server's `notifications/message` arrive, and the SDK's default handler drops them before any caller sees them.
notes_by_num.11: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPClient` opens its `ClientSession` with its own `message_handler` and no `logging_callback`, and takes no log hook, so the server's `notifications/message` never reach the caller.
notes_by_num.12: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: server log messages are delivered only to a `LoggingMessageNotificationSchema` handler set on the SDK client; @genkit-ai/mcp has no API for it and registers no notification handler; it works only on the SDK `Client` that the public getter `GenkitMcpClient.mcpClient` hands out (route `session`).
notes_by_num.13: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the runtime receives the server's `notifications/message` (5 on the wire) but surfaces none of them: no session event fires, and `session.rpc.diagnostics.read` holds only the server's stderr. The caller received 0.
notes_by_num.14: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: reachable only on a raw `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `Client` from `MCPSessionManager.createSession()`, a public export of `@google/adk/tools/mcp`, with `setNotificationHandler(LoggingMessageNotificationSchema)`. The sessions `MCPToolset` opens register no handler, so an agent never sees `notifications/message`.
notes_by_num.15: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: the server options take no message or logging handler. The server sent `notifications/message` and nothing in the SDK received it.
notes_by_num.16: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): MCPClient registers no notification handler: a server notification reaches only `onUncaughtError`, as an "Unsupported message type" error that does not name the notification. The server's five `notifications/message` never reach the caller, and there is no logging option on `createMCPClient`.
notes_by_num.17: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: MCP Java SDK mcp-core 2.0.0 types `LoggingMessageNotification.data` as `String`, so a log notification with object data fails to deserialize (`Cannot deserialize value of type java.lang.String from Object value`); `McpClientSession` logs `Error handling notification` and drops it. The server sent 5 `notifications/message` and the `McpServerLogConsumer` that `McpSessionManager` installs received 0.
notes_by_num.18: Koog 1.3.0-beta: Koog registers no logging handler. `Client.setNotificationHandler(notifications/message)` on the Kotlin SDK `Client` handed to `fromClient` received all 5 messages.
notes_by_num.19: Spring AI 2.0.1: the server's five `notifications/message` arrive on the wire, but MCP Java SDK 2.0.0 types `LoggingMessageNotification.data` as a String. Structured data such as `{"message": ...}` fails to deserialize (`Cannot deserialize value of type java.lang.String from Object value`), `McpClientSession` logs `Error handling notification`, and `@McpLogging` receives none of them.
notes_by_num.20: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): mcptoolset has no logging option. A `mcp.ClientOptions.LoggingMessageHandler` on the `*mcp.Client` the caller passes as `mcptoolset.Config.Client` receives all five `notifications/message`, but only by configuring go-sdk rather than the toolset.

logging-set-level.title: `logging/setLevel`
logging-set-level.description: A request setting the minimum severity the server should emit for the rest of the session.
logging-set-level.question: Does this framework let a caller set the server log level?
logging-set-level.notes: 5 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 14 changed or retained elsewhere, 12 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` has no `logging/setLevel` method; the request works only through `MCPTools.session`, the fastmcp `Client` it exposes (`Client.set_logging_level`).
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: no logging API. `logging/setLevel` is sent only on a `ClientSession` the caller builds and hands `MCPTool.from_client`, which BeeAI uses as given; the session BeeAI opens itself for a transport has no callbacks, via `ClientSession.set_logging_level`.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench` has no `logging/setLevel` method, and its session is private to `McpSessionActor`.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26: `MCPServerAdapter` has no log-level API. Its sessions are private (`_adapter.sessions`) and run on the adapter's own event loop thread.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient` has no log-level API. `logging/setLevel` works only through the public `MCPClient.session` (`session.set_logging_level(...)`), a raw MCP `ClientSession`, which the probe used.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: DSPy has no logging API. `logging/setLevel` works only through `set_logging_level` on the caller's own `mcp.Client`, which DSPy is handed by `Tool.from_mcp_tool` and never configures. DSPy itself offers no route.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK 2.11.0: `McpToolset` has no log-level API. `MCPSessionManager.create_session()` hands out the raw mcp `ClientSession`, and `set_logging_level` on it works.
notes_by_num.8: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPToolset` wraps tools as Haystack `Tool`s and has no resource or prompt API, and the `ClientSession` it opens is private to `MCPToolset._worker._client`, so there is no route to `logging/setLevel`.
notes_by_num.9: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: the adapter has no log-level API of its own. `MultiServerMCPClient.session()` hands out the raw mcp `ClientSession`, and `set_logging_level` on that session works.
notes_by_num.10: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: the adapter has no log-level API of its own. `MultiServerMCPClient.session()` hands out the raw mcp `ClientSession`, and `set_logging_level` on that session works.
notes_by_num.11: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): `BasicMCPClient` has no logging-level method, and its sessions exist only inside the private `_run_session`, so no caller can send `logging/setLevel`.
notes_by_num.12: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: the adapter has no log-level API. `MCPServerStdio.session` is the raw mcp `ClientSession`, and `set_logging_level` on it works.
notes_by_num.13: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `MCPClient` has no log-level API. The session lives on the private `MCPClient._adapter` and runs on the adapter's own event loop thread.
notes_by_num.14: Strands Agents 1.59.0: `MCPClient` has no `logging/setLevel` method, and its `ClientSession` is private (`_background_thread_session`).
notes_by_num.15: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `setLoggingLevel` works and the server honoured it, but @genkit-ai/mcp has no API for it and registers no notification handler; it works only on the SDK `Client` that the public getter `GenkitMcpClient.mcpClient` hands out (route `session`).
notes_by_num.16: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): there is no API that sends `logging/setLevel` or names a log level for an MCP server.
notes_by_num.17: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: reachable only on a raw `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `Client` from `MCPSessionManager.createSession()`, a public export of `@google/adk/tools/mcp` (`setLoggingLevel`). `MCPToolset` has no logging API.
notes_by_num.18: Mastra 2.2.0: `MCPClient` exposes no log-level API. It sets a level per request through `serverLogLevel` instead. The SDK client's `setLoggingLevel` sits behind the private `mcpClientsById` field.
notes_by_num.19: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: `MCPServer` has no `logging/setLevel` method. The MCP client that has `setLoggingLevel` sits in the node shim's `session` field, which the SDK types as protected.
notes_by_num.20: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): `McpClient` has no setLevel method. The public generic `request('logging/setLevel', { level })` reaches the server, which then filters its logs, but the caller names the wire method.
notes_by_num.21: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): MCPClient has no `logging/setLevel` method, and `createMCPClient` offers no public route to send one.
notes_by_num.22: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpClient` has no `logging/setLevel` method, so `DefaultMcpClient` never sends one.
notes_by_num.23: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: No ADK API. `McpTool.getMcpSession().setLoggingLevel` on the underlying `McpSyncClient` works: at `warning` the server sent 2 of 5 messages.
notes_by_num.24: Koog 1.3.0-beta: no Koog API. `Client.setLoggingLevel` on the underlying Kotlin SDK `Client` works: at `warning` the server sent 2 of 5 messages.
notes_by_num.25: Spring AI 2.0.1: the starter's API has no level setter. `McpSyncClient.setLoggingLevel` on the client bean the starter publishes works (at `warning` the server sent 2 of its 5 messages), so this goes through the session rather than the adapter.
notes_by_num.26: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcptoolset.Toolset` exposes only `Tools()`, and the `*mcp.ClientSession` it opens stays inside its unexported `connectionRefresher`, so the caller has no session to call `SetLoggingLevel` on.

pagination-cursor.title: Cursor pagination
pagination-cursor.description: Opaque forward-only cursor paging on every list operation, where the client passes `cursor` and the server returns `nextCursor`.
pagination-cursor.question: Does the framework follow the cursor, or stop after the first page?
pagination-cursor.notes: 19 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 1 changed or retained elsewhere, 11 dropped.

cancellation.title: `notifications/cancelled`
cancellation.description: Abandons an in-flight request, signalled by notification on stdio and by closing the response stream on Streamable HTTP.
cancellation.question: Can the agent abandon a call and have the server hear about it?
cancellation.notes: 16 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 0 changed or retained elsewhere, 15 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: cancelling the asyncio task around `MCPTool.run` abandons the call, but no `notifications/cancelled` is sent, so the server is never told and the request is left unanswered.
notes_by_num.2: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench.call_tool` links the `CancellationToken` to the un-awaited `session.call_tool` coroutine, so `token.cancel()` raises `AttributeError: 'coroutine' object has no attribute 'cancel'`, the call runs to completion, and no `notifications/cancelled` is sent.
notes_by_num.3: CrewAI 1.15.26: a CrewAI tool's `.run()` blocks on the adapter's loop with no timeout or cancel route. `MCPServerAdapter` never passes `client_session_timeout_seconds`, so no timeout applies either.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient.call_tool` has no cancel route. Cancelling the asyncio task around it closes the session without sending `notifications/cancelled`; the only bound is `execution_timeout` (`asyncio.wait_for`), which also abandons the request silently. Each `MCPNativeTool` call opens and closes a fresh `MCPClient`.
notes_by_num.5: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: cancelling the task that awaits `StructuredTool.ainvoke` stops the caller waiting, but the mcp 1.x `ClientSession` sends no `notifications/cancelled`. The server keeps working on the call until the session closes.
notes_by_num.6: LangChain MCP Adapters 0.3.2: cancelling the task that awaits `StructuredTool.ainvoke` stops the caller waiting, but the mcp 1.x `ClientSession` sends no `notifications/cancelled`. The server keeps working on the call until the session closes.
notes_by_num.7: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: cancelling the asyncio task around `MCPTool.call_tool` abandons the call, but no `notifications/cancelled` reaches the server; the request is left unanswered until the session closes.
notes_by_num.8: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: cancelling `Kernel.invoke` abandons the call locally; no `notifications/cancelled` reaches the server.
notes_by_num.9: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): calling a smolagents `Tool` blocks on `asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(...).result()` against the adapter's background loop, and neither `MCPClient` nor the tool offers a cancel route, so no caller can send `notifications/cancelled`.
notes_by_num.10: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `ai.generate({ abortSignal })` is the caller's cancellation hook, but aborting does not reach the MCP request: no `notifications/cancelled` was sent, and the tool call ran on and returned `SENTINEL_NOT_CANCELLED` after about 4 s.
notes_by_num.11: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): a tool's `execute(args, { abortSignal })` rejects with "Request was aborted" when the signal fires, but the client sends no `notifications/cancelled`. The server keeps working and returns SENTINEL_NOT_CANCELLED.
notes_by_num.12: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `McpTool.runAsync` calls the blocking `McpSyncClient.callTool`, and `RunConfig` carries no cancellation signal. Interrupting the thread blocked in `Runner.runAsync` (`Future.cancel(true)`) abandons the wait after 1 s, but no `notifications/cancelled` goes out.
notes_by_num.13: Koog 1.3.0-beta: cancelling the coroutine running `AIAgent.run` abandons the wait after 1 s, but `McpTool.execute` suspends in Kotlin SDK 0.11.1's `Client.callTool`, which sends `notifications/cancelled` only when its own request timeout fires. The wire shows the `tools/call` and no `notifications/cancelled`.
notes_by_num.14: Spring AI 2.0.1: `ToolCallback.call` is synchronous and takes no cancellation signal. Interrupting the calling thread (`Future.cancel(true)`) abandons the wait, but no `notifications/cancelled` goes out; the wire shows the `tools/call` and nothing after it.
notes_by_num.15: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): cancelling the `CancellationToken` passed to `AIAgent.RunAsync` after 1 s ends the run with `TaskCanceledException`, but no `notifications/cancelled` goes out: the server kept working and returned SENTINEL_NOT_CANCELLED for request 6. Calling `McpClient.CallToolAsync` directly with a cancelled token sends none either, so the gap is in the MCP C# SDK, not the agent.

json-schema-dialect.title: JSON Schema dialect
json-schema-dialect.description: The rule that schemas default to JSON Schema 2020-12 unless a `$schema` field declares another dialect, such as draft-07.
json-schema-dialect.question: Does the framework honour the declared dialect, or assume one?
json-schema-dialect.notes: 18 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 7 changed or retained elsewhere, 6 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `JSONSchemaModel.create` runs `simplify_json_schema`, which calls `.items()` on a property's `items` value. A 2020-12 boolean `"items": false` raises `AttributeError: 'bool' object has no attribute 'items'`, and a draft-07 tuple-form `items` list fails the same way, when the agent builds its system prompt. The `RequirementAgent` run then fails for every tool, not only the one with the schema.
notes_by_num.2: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench.list_tools` copies only `properties`, `required` and `additionalProperties`, so `$schema`, `$defs`/`definitions` and `dependentRequired` are dropped, leaving any `$ref` into them dangling.
notes_by_num.3: CrewAI: one draft-07 tool with tuple-form `items` (a list) makes MCPServerAdapter fail to load the whole server (`'list' object has no attribute 'get'` in crewai/utilities/pydantic_schema_utils.py). With that tool left out, the 2020-12 tool is rebuilt through Pydantic: `$schema` and `dependentRequired` are dropped, `prefixItems` becomes `items: {}`, and `$defs` is renamed.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): both dialect tools are offered, but each goes through `create_model_from_schema` and the strict OpenAI schema. The draft-07 tool's tuple `items` fails the Pydantic build, and `MCPToolResolver` logs `Failed to build args schema` and registers the tool with an empty `properties` object, so the model is offered none of its parameters. The 2020-12 tool loses `$schema` and `dependentRequired`, `prefixItems` becomes `items: {}`, and `window`'s `$ref` is inlined. The derived evidence reads "not offered" because the protocol instrument's long launch command pushes every name past 64 characters, so `sanitize_tool_name` hashes away the MCP tool name the cell matches on; the schemas above were read from the same capture in listing order.
notes_by_num.5: DSPy 3.4.0: `convert_input_schema_to_tool_args` keeps only the `inputSchema` properties, inlining `$defs` references. `$schema` and top-level keywords such as `dependentRequired` are dropped, and a draft-07 `definitions` block is dropped with its `$ref`s left dangling.
notes_by_num.6: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): a tool whose `inputSchema` is valid draft-07 but not valid 2020-12 (tuple-form `items`) fails the whole listing: `haystack.tools.Tool` checks every `parameters` with `Draft202012Validator.check_schema` and raises `ValueError: The provided parameters do not define a valid JSON schema`, and `MCPToolset.warm_up` builds every tool in one pass, so no tool loads. The 2020-12 tool kept all eight dialect keywords.
notes_by_num.7: LlamaIndex (llama-index-tools-mcp 0.6.0): with either dialect tool listed, the adapter loads no tool at all. `McpToolSpec` rebuilds each schema as a Pydantic model, and `McpToolSpec._resolve_field_type` fails on both: the 2020-12 tool's boolean subschema (`"items": false`) raises `TypeError: argument of type 'bool' is not iterable`, and the draft-07 tool's tuple `items` list raises `AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'get'`. `to_tool_list_async` builds every tool in one loop, so one such tool fails the listing for the whole server, over stdio and Streamable HTTP. Without both, the other three tools load and are called normally.
notes_by_num.8: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `load_tools` rebuilds `parameters` from `properties` and `required` only, so `$schema`, `$defs`/`definitions` and `dependentRequired` are dropped. Properties that point at a dropped `$defs` entry keep a dangling `$ref`.
notes_by_num.9: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): mcpadapt inlines every `$ref` with `jsonref.replace_refs` and drops `$defs`, and keeps only `inputSchema.properties`, so `$schema`, `definitions` and the 2020-12 tool's `dependentRequired` are gone. `prefixItems`, `items: false` and tuple `items` survive. Because smolagents marks every property required, a 2020-12 call that omits the optional `label` is rejected before it reaches the server (`Argument label is required`).
notes_by_num.10: GitHub Copilot SDK 1.0.19 (Copilot runtime 1.0.95): the runtime rewrites keywords it does not pass to the provider into description text. In the 2020-12 tool, `dependentRequired` becomes `{dependentRequired: {"label":["units"]}}` on the schema's description and `items: false` becomes `{"description": "{schema: false}"}`; in the draft-07 tool the tuple `items` becomes an `anyOf` and `additionalItems: false` likewise turns into a description. `$schema`, `$defs`/`definitions`, `$ref` and `prefixItems` pass through.
notes_by_num.11: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: both dialect tools are listed and called, but `toGeminiSchema` drops what has no genai `Schema` field: `$schema`, `$defs`/`definitions` and `$ref` (the referenced `window` arrives as an empty object), 2020-12 `prefixItems` and `dependentRequired`, and draft-07 tuple `items` and `additionalItems`. Same over stdio and Streamable HTTP (`data/measurements/protocol/google_adk_js/run.json`).
notes_by_num.12: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpToolProvider` maps each `inputSchema` into LangChain4j's own `JsonSchemaElement` model (`JsonObjectSchema`, `JsonStringSchema`, `JsonIntegerSchema`, ...), and the `ToolSpecification` AiServices hands the `ChatModel` is built from that model. The model has no `$schema`, `definitions`, `dependentRequired`, `prefixItems` or `additionalItems`, so both the 2020-12 and draft-07 dialect markers and their keywords are dropped.
notes_by_num.13: Koog 1.3.0-beta: both dialect tools are left out of the registry. `McpToolRegistryProvider.fromClient` catches any `Throwable` from `DefaultMcpToolDescriptorParser.parse` and only logs it, so a tool it cannot parse is left out of the `ToolRegistry`. The 2020-12 tool's `items: false` throws `IllegalArgumentException: Element class kotlinx.serialization.json.JsonLiteral is not a JsonObject`, and the draft-07 tool's tuple-form `items` throws the same for `JsonArray`.

ping.title: `ping`
ping.description: A liveness check either side may send to confirm the peer is still responsive.
ping.question: Does this framework answer or issue a ping?
ping.notes: 30 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 0 changed or retained elsewhere, 1 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `McpOperationHandler` converts every incoming request id to a `long`. A request with a string id, such as the server's `ping` with id `mcp-mirror-ping-1`, is dropped with `Received message with an unusable id` and never answered. Numeric-id pings are answered.

progress-notifications.title: `notifications/progress`
progress-notifications.description: Server-pushed progress updates for a request that opted in by supplying a progress token, reporting a monotonically increasing value with an optional total and message.
progress-notifications.question: Can the agent observe progress on a long-running call?
progress-notifications.notes: 13 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 6 changed or retained elsewhere, 12 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: the fastmcp `Client` sends a `progressToken`, but `MCPTools` takes no progress handler and builds its client without one, so the server's progress notifications reach no caller.
notes_by_num.2: BeeAI Framework 0.1.85: `MCPTool._run` calls `session.call_tool(name, arguments)` with no `progress_callback` and takes none, so no progress token is sent and the server reports no progress.
notes_by_num.3: AutoGen 0.7.5: `McpWorkbench.call_tool` takes no progress callback and sends no `progressToken`.
notes_by_num.4: CrewAI 1.15.26: `MCPServerAdapter` calls `session.call_tool` without a progress callback, so no `progressToken` goes out and the server has nothing to report progress against.
notes_by_num.5: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPClient.call_tool` sends no `progressToken` and takes no progress callback, so the server sends no progress.
notes_by_num.6: DSPy 3.4.0: the `Tool` that `from_mcp_tool` builds calls `session.call_tool(name, arguments=kwargs)` with no `progress_callback` and takes none, so no `progressToken` is sent and the server sends no progress.
notes_by_num.7: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `MCPClient.call_tool` passes no progress callback and `MCPToolset` takes none, so the call carries no `_meta.progressToken` and the server sends no progress.
notes_by_num.8: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: `MCPTool.call_tool` sends no `progressToken` and has no progress callback. Progress works only through `MCPTool.session.call_tool(..., progress_callback=...)` on the raw SDK session.
notes_by_num.9: OpenAI Agents SDK 0.23.1: `invoke_mcp_tool` sends no `progressToken`. Progress works only if the caller passes one by hand, as `call_tool(..., meta={"progressToken": ...})`, and reads the notifications from `message_handler`. No progress callback exists.
notes_by_num.10: Semantic Kernel 1.45.0: `call_tool` passes no progress callback and the plugin takes none, so no progressToken is sent.
notes_by_num.11: smolagents 1.26.0 (mcpadapt 0.1.20): `MCPClient` takes no progress callback and mcpadapt calls `session.call_tool` without one, so no `progressToken` goes out and the server has nothing to report progress against.
notes_by_num.12: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: the tool action calls `callTool` without `onprogress`, so the caller never sees progress through Genkit; `callTool(params, undefined, { onprogress })` on the SDK client delivers all five. @genkit-ai/mcp has no API for it and registers no notification handler; it works only on the SDK `Client` that the public getter `GenkitMcpClient.mcpClient` hands out (route `session`).
notes_by_num.13: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: reachable only on a raw `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` `Client` from `MCPSessionManager.createSession()`, a public export of `@google/adk/tools/mcp`, by passing `onprogress` to `callTool`. `MCPTool.runAsync` calls `callTool(params, undefined, { signal })` with no `onprogress`, so an agent's tool call never sends a progress token.
notes_by_num.14: OpenAI Agents SDK (JS) 0.20.0: a `progressToken` can be sent through the documented `toolMetaResolver` option, and the server then sends progress, but no SDK hook receives `notifications/progress`, so the caller sees none of it.
notes_by_num.15: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): `RequestOptions` takes only `signal`, `timeout` and `maxTotalTimeout`, so `tools/call` carries no `_meta.progressToken` and the server sends no progress.
notes_by_num.16: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `McpSessionManager` builds the `McpSyncClient` with empty client capabilities and no `progressConsumer`, and neither `McpToolset` nor `McpTool` takes one, so `McpTool.runAsync` sends no `progressToken` and no progress reaches the caller.
notes_by_num.17: Koog 1.3.0-beta: no route. `McpTool.execute` calls `Client.callTool(name, arguments)` with no `RequestOptions.onProgress`, so no `progressToken` is sent, and `McpToolRegistryProvider` takes no progress callback.
notes_by_num.18: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): `mcpTool.Run` calls `CallTool` with `Name` and `Arguments` only, so `tools/call` carries no `_meta.progressToken` and the server sends no progress. A `ProgressNotificationHandler` on the caller's `*mcp.Client` never fires.

session-identifier.title: `Mcp-Session-Id`
session-identifier.description: A server-minted session header that binds subsequent Streamable HTTP requests to server-side state.
session-identifier.question: Does this framework return the session header on later requests?
session-identifier.notes: 30 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 1 changed or retained elsewhere, 0 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): every request after initialize carried the minted Mcp-Session-Id. The one rejected request is the SSE GET the client opens before initialize on its second connection (render, then render_result), right after its server/discover probe failed; no session existed yet on that connection. The rule counts it because the first connection had already minted an ID.

sse-resumability.title: `Last-Event-ID` resumability
sse-resumability.description: Stream resumption in which a client reconnects with the last event id it saw and the server redelivers what it missed.
sse-resumability.question: Does this framework resume a broken stream rather than losing the request?
sse-resumability.notes: 24 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 5 changed or retained elsewhere, 2 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73): when the sse-retry scenario closed the SSE stream, the client reconnected (client-sse-graceful-reconnect passed) but sent no Last-Event-ID header (client-sse-last-event-id, a SHOULD), so events sent while it was disconnected are not replayed. The suite also recorded it reconnecting before the server's retry interval, which does not decide this cell, and the tool call then did not return within the renderer's 90-second timeout.
notes_by_num.2: LangChain.js (@langchain/mcp-adapters 2.0.1): in the conformance `sse-retry` scenario the Streamable HTTP client reconnects but does not send `Last-Event-ID` and does not honour the server's `retry` timing (1 of 3 checks passed).
notes_by_num.3: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: when the server closes a tool call's SSE stream, `StreamableHttpMcpTransport` never reconnects with a `GET` (the conformance `sse-retry` scenario counts 0 reconnections), and the call ends in `There was a timeout executing the tool`.
notes_by_num.4: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `sse-retry`: the MCP Java SDK 2.0.0 client reconnects with GET after a graceful close (pass), but it reconnects without waiting the server's 500 ms `retry` (`client-sse-retry-timing` fails) and sends no `Last-Event-ID` (warning).
notes_by_num.5: Spring AI 2.0.1: in the conformance `sse-retry` scenario the client reconnects with GET after a graceful close, but it does not wait the server's `retry` interval (`client-sse-retry-timing` fails) and sends no `Last-Event-ID` (warning).
notes_by_num.6: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) 1.24.0 (ModelContextProtocol 2.2.0): in the conformance `sse-retry` scenario `McpClient.CreateAsync` fails before any tool call: it sends `server/discover` first, cannot deserialize the reply as a `DiscoverResult` (`supportedVersions` and `capabilities` missing) and does not fall back to `initialize`, so the GET reconnect is never reached.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK (Go) 2.5.0 (go-sdk 1.8.0): in the conformance `sse-retry` scenario the go-sdk Streamable HTTP client reconnects, but too early (-128 ms against a 500 ms `retry`), and sends no `Last-Event-ID`.

transport-http-sse.notes: 24 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 1 changed or retained elsewhere, 6 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): the session opens and calls work, but the tool names change with the transport: over HTTP+SSE each tool is named after the URL's host, port and path (`127_0_0_1_<port>_sse_search_records`), so the name differs from the stdio one and from run to run as the port changes.
notes_by_num.2: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.21.0: the adapter ships `MCPStdioTool`, `MCPStreamableHTTPTool` and `MCPWebsocketTool`; there is no HTTP+SSE client, so a legacy `/sse` server cannot be reached.
notes_by_num.3: Genkit (JS) 1.42.0: `transportFrom` accepts `{ command }` (stdio), `{ url }` (Streamable HTTP) or a custom `transport`; there is no HTTP+SSE variant.
notes_by_num.4: Google ADK (TypeScript) 2.2.1: `MCPConnectionParams` is `StdioConnectionParams` or `StreamableHTTPConnectionParams`; there is no HTTP+SSE variant.
notes_by_num.5: Mastra 2.2.0: `@mastra/mcp` builds only a `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` for a URL server and has no HTTP+SSE client. Pointed at the legacy `/sse` endpoint it POSTs there, gets 405 Method Not Allowed, and fails to connect instead of falling back to `GET /sse`.
notes_by_num.6: Pi (@earendil-works/pi-mcp 1.1.0): the package ships `StdioTransport` and `StreamableHttpTransport` only; its README lists legacy HTTP+SSE as outside the core, so no session opens against an HTTP+SSE server.
notes_by_num.7: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: langchain4j-mcp ships stdio, Streamable HTTP and WebSocket transports. The deprecated HTTP+SSE transport is gone, so no session opens.

transport-streamable-http.title: Streamable HTTP transport
transport-streamable-http.description: One HTTP POST per message to a single endpoint, answered with a JSON object or a request-scoped SSE stream, and carrying the required `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` headers.
transport-streamable-http.question: Can the framework talk to a remote server on this revision's terms?
transport-streamable-http.notes: 30 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 1 changed or retained elsewhere, 0 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): the session opens and lists the same definitions as stdio, but on the pinned Python 3.11 every tool call fails. `MCPNativeTool._run` calls `asyncio.run` when no event loop is running, which is the case for `BaseTool.run` and for a synchronous crew, and the fresh `MCPClient` it opens for the call then fails to close its `streamablehttp_client` transport: `RuntimeError: Error executing MCP tool text_content: Error during MCP client disconnect: no running event loop`, for all 18 calls at both boundaries. The server did answer each `tools/call`; the result is lost on the client. A standalone repro of the same call succeeds on Python 3.12 and 3.13, and on 3.11 when the tool runs inside a running event loop; neither was measured by the instrument. The tool names also change with the transport: each is named after the URL's host, port and path (`127_0_0_1_<port>_mcp_search_records`), so the name differs from the stdio one and from run to run as the port changes.

authorization-oauth.title: OAuth 2.1 authorization
authorization-oauth.description: Transport-level OAuth 2.1 for HTTP transports, including the RFC 8707 `resource` parameter on both authorization and token requests.
authorization-oauth.question: Can the framework authorize against a protected MCP server?
authorization-oauth.notes: 0 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 0 changed or retained elsewhere, 0 dropped, 31 unmeasured. No scan probes this feature yet. It is published because the specification defines it, not because anything is known about how adapters handle it.
authorization-oauth.summary: No scan probes this feature yet. It is published because the specification defines it, not because anything is known about how adapters handle it.

verdict.headline: Not yet measured.
verdict.detail: Point each adapter at an OAuth-protected fixture and inspect the authorization requests it makes.

authorization-oauth.why: Almost every hosted MCP server is protected, so this row decides whether a framework can reach real servers or only local ones. The `resource` parameter is what binds a token to one server; omitting it produces tokens that a careful server will refuse and a careless one will over-accept.
authorization-oauth.probe: Point each adapter at an OAuth-protected fixture and inspect the authorization requests it makes.

authorization-resource-metadata.title: Protected Resource Metadata
authorization-resource-metadata.description: RFC 9728 discovery, where the server advertises its authorization server through a `WWW-Authenticate` challenge and clients follow it rather than being configured by hand.
authorization-resource-metadata.question: Does the framework discover the authorization server from the challenge?
authorization-resource-metadata.notes: 22 of 31 frameworks present at the capture boundary, 1 changed or retained elsewhere, 8 dropped.

notes_by_num.1: Agno 3.1.2: `MCPTools` takes only static `headers` or a `header_provider` and builds its HTTP transport with `auth=None`, so it never fetches protected-resource or authorization-server metadata.
notes_by_num.2: AutoGen 0.7.5: No auth hook (see Authorization): the workbench never fetches protected-resource or authorization-server metadata.
notes_by_num.3: CrewAI 1.15.26, native `crewai.mcp` client (`Agent(mcps=[...])`, not the `crewai_tools.MCPServerAdapter` row): `MCPServerHTTP` and `MCPServerSSE` take only `url` and static `headers`, and `HTTPTransport` calls `streamablehttp_client` with no `auth`, so the client does no OAuth discovery: in the conformance suite's auth scenarios it never fetched the protected resource metadata or the authorization server metadata.
notes_by_num.4: Haystack (mcp-haystack 1.5.2): `StreamableHttpServerInfo` and `SSEServerInfo` take a static `token` or `headers`, and `MCPClient` builds its httpx client with no auth handler, so the adapter does no OAuth discovery: it never fetched the protected resource metadata or the authorization server metadata in the conformance suite's auth scenarios.
notes_by_num.5: Vercel AI SDK (@ai-sdk/mcp 2.0.73, an OAuthClientProvider as the HTTP transport's authProvider, conformance suite 0.1.16): discovery passed in metadata-default, var1 and var2. In metadata-var3, where the authorization server's URL has a path, the client also requested that server's metadata at the root path (authorization-server-metadata-wrong-path, 5 of 8 checks passed).
notes_by_num.6: LangChain4j 1.22.0-beta32: `StreamableHttpMcpTransport` takes static `customHeaders` or an `McpHeadersSupplier`, and langchain4j-mcp ships no OAuth client. It never fetches protected-resource or authorization-server metadata.
notes_by_num.7: Google ADK (Java) 1.11.0: `StreamableHttpServerParameters` and `SseServerParameters` take only static headers, and ADK has no OAuth hook. Every `auth/*` conformance scenario fails: the client sends no `Authorization` header, the server answers 401, and `McpToolset.getTools` throws `McpToolLoadingException` (cause: `McpHttpClientTransportAuthorizationException`).
notes_by_num.8: Koog 1.3.0-beta: no OAuth flow, so the client never requests protected resource metadata or authorization server metadata after the 401.
notes_by_num.9: Spring AI 2.0.1: the starter has no OAuth hook; Spring AI points OAuth users at the separate community module `mcp-client-security`. Against the conformance auth scenarios the client sends no Authorization header, never fetches protected-resource metadata, and fails to start on the server's 401.

known_issues: Measured with the official MCP conformance suite 0.1.16, whose client scenarios are tagged 2025-11-25.
authorization-resource-metadata.why: This is what makes connecting to an unfamiliar protected server possible without out-of-band setup. A framework that requires hand-configured endpoints cannot connect to a server it was not told about in advance, and cannot handle a step-up scope challenge when one arrives.
